c: A taking requiring compensation
A valid use of police power with no payment
An easement by necessity
A special assessment
questions.x: Regulation that goes too far, such as wiping out all economic use, counts as a taking and compensation is owed. Police power is the trap: ordinary zoning needs no payment, but not when it takes everything.

questions.q: Government action is treated as a 'taking' when it:
c: Raises the property tax rate
Requires a building permit
Occupies property or regulates it too far
Adopts a new master plan
questions.x: Physical occupation or excessive regulation triggers just compensation. A building permit is the trap: routine permitting is not a taking.

questions.q: A nonpossessory right to use another person's land for a specific purpose is a(n):
c: Lease
Easement
License to occupy
Life estate
questions.x: Easements give use, not possession. Lease is the trap: a lease gives possession.

questions.q: A utility's right to run power lines across a back yard is a(n):
c: Encroachment
Fee simple
Deed restriction
Easement
questions.x: The utility holds a right to use the land: an easement. Encroachment is the trap: that is an unauthorized intrusion.

questions.q: The right to pass over another person's land to reach your own is a:
c: Riparian right
Lien
Right-of-way
Variance
questions.x: A right-of-way is an easement to cross land. Variance is the trap: it is permission to depart from zoning.

questions.q: A strip of land used for a railroad line is commonly called a:
c: Right-of-way
Cul-de-sac
Buffer zone
Setback
questions.x: Strips for roads, rails and utilities are rights-of-way. Setback is the trap: it is a required distance from a lot line.

questions.q: A New York municipality's official map shows a proposed street through Lot 9. The owner generally:
c: Must sell the lot at once
Is exempt from property tax
May build anything with a permit
Cannot build in the mapped street bed
questions.x: Building in a mapped street bed is generally barred, which protects the planned street. 'Must sell at once' is the trap: mapping is not an immediate taking.

questions.q: An official map adopted by a municipality shows:
c: Every property's assessed value
Existing and proposed streets, parks and drainage
Flood insurance rates
School district test scores
questions.x: The official map fixes streets, parks and drainage, existing and planned. Assessed values are the trap: those are on the assessment roll.

questions.q: A dead-end street that ends in a circular turnaround is a:
c: Cul-de-sac
Gridiron street
Arterial road
Right-of-way
questions.x: That is the definition of a cul-de-sac. Gridiron is the trap: it is a pattern of straight, crossing streets.

questions.q: Subdivision designers use cul-de-sacs mainly to:
c: Increase lot density
Speed up commuting
Reduce through traffic
Avoid drainage rules
questions.x: Dead ends keep through traffic out. Speeding up commuting is the trap: cul-de-sacs do the opposite.

questions.q: Roads, water, sewer, power and schools that support development are together called:
c: Topography
Infrastructure
Amenities
Demography
questions.x: Infrastructure is the public systems that make development possible. Topography is the trap: it is the land's surface features.

questions.q: A planner says a new subdivision can't be approved until sewer capacity is added. The concern is:
c: Demography
Topography
Zoning density only
Infrastructure
questions.x: Sewer capacity is infrastructure. Demography is the trap: that is population data.

questions.q: The study of population characteristics such as age, income and household size is:
c: Topography
Geography
Demography
Ecology
questions.x: Demography studies population. Topography is the trap: it studies land surfaces.

questions.q: A developer checks how many young families live in an area before building 3-bedroom homes. This is:
c: Demographic research
A topographic survey
A title search
A soil test
questions.x: Household and age data are demographics. Topographic survey is the trap: it maps elevation.

questions.q: A small statistical area defined by the U.S. Census Bureau, usually 1,200 to 8,000 people, is a:
c: Zoning district
School district
Tax map block
Census tract
questions.x: Census tracts are the Bureau's small reporting areas. Zoning district is the trap: that is a local land-use category.

questions.q: Census tracts are mainly used to:
c: Set property tax rates
Report population and housing data
Draw legislative maps for zoning
Assign mortgage rates
questions.x: They are statistical units for data reporting. Property tax rates are the trap: those are set by taxing jurisdictions.

questions.q: The elevation, slope and natural features of land are its:
c: Topography
Demography
Infrastructure
Zoning
questions.x: Topography describes the surface of the land. Demography is the trap: it describes people.

questions.q: Steep slopes and wetlands on a site are part of its:
c: Census profile
Title chain
Topography
Assessment
questions.x: Physical surface features are topography. Title chain is the trap: it is ownership history.

questions.q: A licensed professional's map of a parcel's boundaries, improvements and encroachments is a:
c: Title search
Survey
Appraisal
Plat of subdivision only
questions.x: A survey measures and maps the parcel. Title search is the trap: it reviews records, not the ground.

questions.q: Which would best reveal that a neighbor's fence sits 2 feet onto the property?
c: A title search
An appraisal
A home inspection
A survey
questions.x: Surveys find encroachments on the ground. A title search is the trap: an unrecorded fence won't appear in the records.

questions.q: Which New York agency houses the State Historic Preservation Office and the State and National Registers of Historic Places?
c: Department of State
Department of Environmental Conservation
Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation
Division of Housing and Community Renewal
questions.x: OPRHP runs state parks and historic sites and houses SHPO. The Department of State is the trap: it licenses real estate agents.

questions.q: An owner wants to know whether her building is on the State Register of Historic Places. She should check with:
c: OPRHP's preservation office
The county clerk
DOS licensing
The local zoning board
questions.x: The State Historic Preservation Office within OPRHP keeps the registers. The county clerk is the trap: it records deeds.

questions.q: A building that complies with every zoning rule for its district and needs only a building permit is built:
c: By variance
By special permit
As a nonconforming use
As of right
questions.x: As-of-right projects need no discretionary approval. Variance is the trap: that is relief from rules the project breaks.

questions.q: Which project needs no zoning board approval?
c: One needing an area variance
One that meets all zoning rules as of right
One needing a special use permit
One changing the zoning map
questions.x: Compliant projects proceed with just a building permit. Special permit is the trap: it requires discretionary review.

questions.q: A secondary unit within a single-family home, often allowed only if the owner lives on site, is a(n):
c: Accessory apartment
Illegal conversion
Two-family dwelling
Co-op unit
questions.x: Many municipalities permit accessory apartments by permit, often with owner occupancy. Two-family dwelling is the trap: that is a different zoning classification.

questions.q: A common condition for a permitted accessory apartment is that:
c: It has its own tax lot
It is rent stabilized
The owner lives on the property
It is sold separately
questions.x: Owner occupancy is a frequent requirement. Its own tax lot is the trap: the unit stays part of the single lot.

questions.q: Owners whose lots touch the property seeking a variance usually receive notice because they are:
c: Grantees
Abutting owners
Lienholders
Assessors
questions.x: Abutting means sharing a boundary, and neighbors usually get hearing notice. Grantees is the trap: that means people receiving a deed.

questions.q: 'Abutting' means:
c: Within one mile
In the same zip code
Across the street only
Touching or sharing a boundary
questions.x: Abutting properties touch. 'Within one mile' is the trap: that is nearby, not abutting.

questions.q: Zoning ordinances, building codes, and subdivision regulations are all exercises of the government's:
c: Police power
Eminent domain
Escheat power
Taxing power
questions.x: Regulating land use for health, safety and welfare is police power, and no compensation is owed. The tempting trap is eminent domain, which takes title to property and must pay just compensation.

questions.q: The legal process by which government acquires private property for public use is called:
c: Escheat
Condemnation
Dedication
Adverse possession
questions.x: Condemnation is the court procedure for exercising eminent domain, and the owner receives just compensation. Escheat also moves land to the state, but only when an owner dies with no will and no heirs.

questions.q: All of the following are government powers over private land EXCEPT:
c: Property taxation
Escheat to the state
Deed restrictions
Eminent domain
questions.x: Deed restrictions (restrictive covenants) are private controls created by a deed or a developer's declaration. Taxation, escheat, eminent domain and police power (PETE) are the four government powers; escheat is the one candidates forget.

questions.q: When a person dies with no will and no heirs, title to the person's real property passes to the state by:
c: Condemnation
Adverse possession
Dedication
Escheat
questions.x: Escheat sends property to the state when there is no one to inherit. Condemnation also moves land to government, but it requires a public use and payment of just compensation.

questions.q: A subdivision's recorded declaration bans fences in front yards. The town's zoning code allows front fences up to 4 feet. An owner wants a 3-foot front fence. Which is correct?
c: She may build it, since public zoning overrides a private covenant
She may not build it, since the stricter covenant controls
She may build it once the ZBA grants an area variance
She may build it, since a covenant that conflicts with zoning is void
questions.x: When public and private controls differ, the more restrictive one governs. The variance option is the trap: a ZBA can relax zoning, but it has no power to waive a private covenant.

questions.q: Neighbors knew for eight years that a homeowner violated a deed restriction and did nothing. A court may refuse to enforce the restriction now under:
c: The doctrine of laches
Escheat to the state
The Statute of Frauds
Estoppel by deed
questions.x: Laches bars a claim when unreasonable delay in asserting a right has prejudiced the other party. Estoppel by deed is a title doctrine about after-acquired title, not delay in enforcing a covenant.

questions.q: In New York, zoning must be adopted in accordance with a:
c: Federal property report
Comprehensive plan
Certificate of occupancy
Recorded subdivision plat
questions.x: State law requires zoning to follow a comprehensive (master) plan, the community's long-range blueprint. A subdivision plat is a map of one tract; it does not authorize zoning for the whole municipality.

questions.q: The local board that typically reviews and approves subdivision plats and site plans in a New York town is the:
c: Zoning board of appeals
Board of assessment review
Town planning board
County board of health
questions.x: The planning board handles subdivision and site plan review and advises on the master plan. The ZBA is the common wrong pick: it grants variances and interprets the ordinance, not plats.

questions.q: A town board adopts a 6-month pause on approving new subdivisions while it updates its comprehensive plan. This is best described as:
c: A taking that requires just compensation
Spot zoning of the affected parcels
A use variance granted to the town
A valid temporary moratorium
questions.x: A reasonable, temporary moratorium tied to planning is a valid police power tool. It risks being a compensable taking only if it is unreasonably long or eliminates all economic use.

questions.q: Under SEQRA, if the lead agency determines that a proposed action may have a significant adverse environmental impact, it issues a:
c: Negative declaration
Positive declaration
Conditioned negative declaration
Findings statement
questions.x: A positive declaration triggers a full environmental impact statement. A negative declaration (conditioned or not) means no significant impact, and a findings statement comes at the end of the EIS process, not the start.

questions.q: New York's Article 9-A of the Real Property Law requires a subdivider to file an offering statement with the Department of State before offering:
c: Vacant subdivided lots to NY buyers on installment terms
Condominium units in a new New York City building
Commercial space under leases running longer than 10 years
Homes in a planned unit development sold to cash buyers
questions.x: Article 9-A targets vacant subdivided land sold to New Yorkers on installment plans, a classic area for lot-sale abuse. Condominium offerings are filed with the Attorney General under different law.

questions.q: Under the Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act, a buyer who receives the property report before signing may revoke the contract within:
c: 3 days
10 days
7 days
30 days
questions.x: The Act gives a 7-day cooling-off right after signing. The 3-day number belongs to the TILA right of rescission on refinances, and 10 days is the lead-paint testing window.

questions.q: Which document certifies that a completed building complies with codes and may be lawfully occupied for its stated use?
c: Building permit and plans
Certificate of title
Final inspection report
Certificate of occupancy
questions.x: The CO is issued after final inspection. A building permit only authorizes construction to begin, so it says nothing about whether the finished building may be occupied.

questions.q: New York's Open Meetings Law requires a town planning board to do all of the following EXCEPT:
c: Hold its meetings open to the public
Give advance notice of meetings
Keep minutes of its meetings
Let attendees vote on applications
questions.x: The public may attend and observe and is entitled to notice and minutes, but votes belong to board members. The law guarantees transparency, not public voting.

questions.q: A New York City law required a landlord to let a cable company install a small box on her roof. The U.S. Supreme Court held this was:
c: A taking, because the occupation was permanent
Not a taking, because the box occupied so little space
Not a taking, because it was a valid police power rule
A taking, but one that requires no compensation
questions.x: Loretto v. Teleprompter (1982) held that a permanent physical occupation authorized by government is a taking regardless of size. The police power answer is the trap: that reasoning saved landmark rules in Penn Central, which involved no physical occupation.

questions.q: A town's zoning law limits what Evelyn may build on her land. In bundle-of-rights terms, which is true?
c: The town now holds part of her legal title
She is owed compensation for the lost use
Her deed is void until she gets a permit
She owns it; only the use is limited
questions.x: Owning land means holding a bundle of rights (possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion, disposition), and none is absolute. Zoning trims the use sticks without taking title, so no compensation is owed, which is the trap.

questions.q: The bundle of rights includes each of the following EXCEPT:
c: Escheat
Possession
Exclusion
Disposition
questions.x: The bundle is possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion and disposition. Escheat is one of the government's four powers (PETE), on the other side of the ledger.

questions.q: A subdivision's recorded declaration bars commercial kennels. A later buyer of a lot who never signed the declaration:
c: Is free of it, having never signed it personally
Is bound if the town's zoning also bans kennels
Is bound, since the covenant runs with the land
Is bound for 10 years, after which it lapses
questions.x: Covenants in a recorded declaration run with the land and bind future owners, whether or not they signed. Thinking only the original signer is bound is the trap.

questions.q: Neighbors in a subdivision want to stop a lot owner from violating a recorded covenant. They typically enforce it through:
c: A complaint to the building inspector
An appeal to the zoning board of appeals
A petition to the planning board
A lawsuit seeking an injunction
questions.x: Private covenants are enforced by neighbors or the HOA in court, usually by injunction. Building inspectors and the ZBA enforce public zoning, not private deed restrictions.

questions.q: A developer wants approval for townhouses, shops and a park planned together on one tract with flexible lot lines. The best fit is a:
c: Site plan review approval
Use variance from the ZBA
Planned unit development
Spot zoning change
questions.x: A PUD approves a whole tract as one mixed project, often with flexible lots and shared open space. Site plan review looks at the layout of a single project on one lot.

questions.q: Site plan review by a planning board focuses on:
c: Splitting raw land into separate building lots
One project's parking, lighting and access
Whether a prohibited use may be allowed
A town's long-range land use blueprint
questions.x: Site plan review approves the layout of a single project, such as parking, landscaping, lighting, access and drainage. Splitting land into lots is subdivision review, the closest neighbor.

questions.q: Under SEQRA, an application to build one single-family home is typically:
c: A Type II action needing no review
A Type I action requiring an EIS
An unlisted action needing an EAF
Exempt, but only outside New York City
questions.x: Type II actions, such as a single-family home or a side-yard variance, need no SEQRA review. Type I and unlisted actions are reviewed, starting with an Environmental Assessment Form.

questions.q: New York City carries out SEQRA through:
c: City Environmental Quality Review
The Uniform Land Use Review Procedure
The Board of Standards and Appeals
The Interstate Land Sales Act rules
questions.x: NYC implements SEQRA through CEQR: same idea, city procedures. ULURP is the city's land use approval process, which often runs alongside CEQR but is not the environmental review.

questions.q: Which statement about building codes in New York State is correct?
c: Each town writes its own code with no state minimum
A statewide code applies; towns may be stricter
Building codes are set by the federal government
NYC must follow the state code with no changes
questions.x: NY has a statewide Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code, administered by DOS and enforced locally, and municipalities may adopt stricter rules. NYC has its own Construction Codes, so 'no changes' is wrong.

questions.q: The New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code is administered by the:
c: Department of Health
Local planning board
Department of State
Federal HUD office
questions.x: The Department of State administers the Uniform Code, and cities, towns and villages enforce it. Planning boards review plats and site plans, not code compliance.

questions.q: Schools, hospitals and houses of worship usually fall in which zoning classification?
c: Commercial
Public open space
Agricultural
Institutional
questions.x: Institutional districts cover schools, hospitals and houses of worship. Public open space covers parks, beaches and preserved land, the closest wrong answer.

questions.q: Which zoning classification gets extra protection under NY law from local rules that unreasonably restrict its use?
c: Industrial districts
Vacant land holdings
Agricultural districts
Institutional districts
questions.x: NY agricultural districts are protected from local laws that unreasonably restrict farming. Industrial districts hold manufacturing and warehouses but get no such special state protection.

questions.q: A tutor runs a small business from her house in a residential zone, with limits on employees and signs. This is a:
c: Home occupation
Nonconforming use
Accessory apartment
Use variance
questions.x: A home occupation is a small business inside a dwelling, usually limited in employees, signs and floor area. A nonconforming use predates the zoning, which this does not.

questions.q: Zoning limits on a home occupation commonly restrict each of the following EXCEPT:
c: The number of employees on site
The size of any signs
The floor area it uses
The owner's income from it
questions.x: Home occupation rules typically limit employees, signs and floor area to protect the neighborhood. Zoning regulates land use, not how much the owner earns.

questions.q: A town defines 'family' to exclude unrelated people living together as one household. NY's highest court has:
c: Upheld them as police power
Struck down such definitions
Required a use variance first
Left the issue to each town
questions.x: NY's highest court has struck down family definitions that exclude unrelated people living as the functional equivalent of a family. Upholding them as a valid police power use is the trap.

questions.q: Why do zoning codes define 'family'?
c: To decide which heirs inherit property by escheat
To control occupancy of single-family districts
To set tax rates for each household
To limit how many cars may park on a lot
questions.x: Zoning defines family to control occupancy in single-family districts. Escheat and taxes are separate government powers that do not depend on the zoning definition.

questions.q: A contractor keeps building after a permit problem is found. Who issues the stop-work order?
c: The zoning board of appeals
The county board of health
The town planning board
The building department
questions.x: The building department (building inspector or code enforcement officer) issues permits and COs, inspects, and writes stop-work orders. The ZBA hears appeals; it does not police job sites.

questions.q: A house's well and septic system raise sanitary questions. Which body usually oversees them?
c: The board of health, often county
The zoning board of appeals
The town justice court
The State Historic Preservation Office
questions.x: Boards of health, often at the county level, handle wells, septic and sanitary issues. Town and village justice courts hear code violation charges but do not oversee septic systems.

questions.q: New York City's City of Yes for Housing Opportunity, adopted in December 2024, among other things:
c: Abolished ULURP for all rezonings
Banned accessory dwelling units on one-family lots
Ended parking mandates for much new housing
Moved variance power from the BSA to the Council
questions.x: City of Yes ended required parking for new housing in much of the city and allows accessory dwelling units on many one and two family lots. 'Banned ADUs' reverses the actual change.

questions.q: Under City of Yes (2024), many NYC one and two family lots may now add:
c: A ground-floor commercial storefront
Unlimited building height
A transfer of air rights
An accessory dwelling unit
questions.x: City of Yes allows accessory dwelling units on many one and two family lots. It did not lift height limits or add storefronts to residential lots.

questions.q: A village adopts a code requiring smoke detectors on every floor of existing homes and pays owners nothing. The village is relying on its:
c: Power of eminent domain
Police power
Power of escheat
Power of taxation
questions.x: Rules protecting health and safety are police power, and the government owes no compensation for them. Eminent domain is the trap: it applies when government takes property, and then it must pay.

questions.q: The state needs a strip of a farm to widen a highway. The farmer refuses to sell. The state files suit to take the strip and pay its value. This proceeding is:
c: Escheat
Dedication
Condemnation
Inverse condemnation
questions.x: Condemnation is the government's lawsuit to take property under eminent domain and pay just compensation. Inverse condemnation is the reverse: the owner sues because government took or damaged property without starting a proceeding.

questions.q: Which of the following is a private land use control rather than a government power?
c: Escheat
Police power
Eminent domain
A restrictive covenant
questions.x: A restrictive covenant is created privately by deed or a developer's declaration and enforced by other owners. Escheat sounds obscure, which tempts guessers, but it is one of the four government powers (PETE).

questions.q: An owner dies without a will. A search finds no spouse, children, or other relatives. Her house will go to the state through:
c: Escheat
Condemnation
A tax foreclosure
Adverse possession
questions.x: Escheat transfers property to the state when no heirs exist. A tax foreclosure also moves land to government, but it happens because taxes went unpaid, not because the owner died without heirs.

questions.q: Zoning requires a 40-foot front setback. A recorded covenant in the same subdivision requires only 25 feet. An owner wants to build 30 feet from the front line. Which is correct?
c: He may build there, as the covenant allows 25 feet
He may not build there, because zoning is stricter here
He may build there if the HOA board signs a waiver
He may not build there unless the covenant is amended
questions.x: The more restrictive control governs, and here the stricter one is zoning. The covenant answer is the trap: a lenient private covenant cannot authorize what public zoning forbids.

questions.q: A neighbor watched a carport go up in violation of a deed restriction, said nothing for nine years, and then sued to have it removed. The owner's best defense is:
c: Laches
Spot zoning
Adverse possession of the covenant
The Statute of Frauds
questions.x: Laches lets a court refuse relief when a party sat on a known right and the delay hurt the other side. Adverse possession tempts because of the long time period, but it is a way to gain title to land, not to defeat a covenant.

questions.q: A town rezones land with no study and no link to its long-range goals. Opponents argue the rezoning is invalid in New York because it is not consistent with the town's:
c: Comprehensive plan
Official tax map
Building code
Subdivision regulations
questions.x: New York requires zoning to be in accordance with a comprehensive plan. Subdivision regulations govern how a tract is divided into lots; they are not the yardstick for a zoning change.

questions.q: A builder wants to split a 12-acre parcel into 18 house lots in a Westchester town. The builder first submits the plat for approval to the:
c: Zoning board of appeals
Town planning board
Building department
County clerk's office
questions.x: Subdivision plats go to the planning board for review and approval. The county clerk records the approved plat afterward, which is why that choice tempts, but recording is not approval.

questions.q: A temporary moratorium on new building permits is most likely to be struck down as a taking when it:
c: Lasts six months while a plan is updated
Is adopted after a public hearing
Runs indefinitely and blocks all use
Applies to commercial projects alone
questions.x: A moratorium becomes vulnerable when it is unreasonably long or denies all economically beneficial use. A short pause tied to planning, the first choice, is the classic valid moratorium.

questions.q: Under SEQRA, a lead agency's negative declaration means that:
c: A full environmental impact statement is required
The project is denied on environmental grounds
No significant adverse impact is expected
The applicant has to pick another lead agency
questions.x: A negative declaration finds no significant adverse impact, so no EIS is needed. The EIS choice describes a positive declaration, the opposite finding.

questions.q: New York's Article 9-A subdivided land law is aimed at each of the following features EXCEPT:
c: Lots sold to New York residents
Vacant, undeveloped subdivided land
Sales paid for on installment plans
Condominium units in NYC towers
questions.x: Article 9-A covers vacant subdivided land offered to New Yorkers on installment terms, filed with the Department of State. Condominium offerings fall under the Attorney General's offering plan rules instead.

questions.q: A New Yorker signs a contract for a lot in a 150-lot Arizona subdivision covered by the Interstate Land Sales Act. Five days later she changes her mind. She:
c: Can revoke, since the 7-day period is still open
Cannot revoke, since the 3-day period has passed
Cannot revoke, because a signed lot sale is final
Cannot revoke unless the developer consents
questions.x: The Act gives buyers 7 days after signing to revoke. The 3-day number is borrowed from TILA's rescission right on refinances, which does not apply to a lot purchase.

questions.q: A buyer's attorney wants proof that a finished basement apartment was legally approved for living use. The attorney should ask for the:
c: Certificate of occupancy
Original building permit
Most recent tax bill
Contractor's final invoice
questions.x: The CO states the legal use and occupancy of the building after final inspection. A building permit tempts, but it only authorized work to start and proves nothing about final approval.

questions.q: A town zoning board of appeals meets privately at a member's home, gives no notice, and votes on a variance. Under New York's Open Meetings Law, the board:
c: Acted properly since a quorum was present
Violated the law by deliberating in secret
Acted properly since it is quasi-judicial
Acted properly if minutes were filed later
questions.x: Public bodies, including ZBAs and planning boards, must meet in public with advance notice. Being quasi-judicial lets a board deliberate privately in narrow cases, but it does not excuse an unnoticed meeting and vote.

questions.q: Which government action is a taking requiring compensation no matter how small the economic loss?
c: A landmark law limiting facade changes
A zoning change cutting allowed density
A required permanent cable box on a roof
A six-month moratorium on new permits
questions.x: Under Loretto, any permanent physical occupation authorized by government is a per se taking. Landmark limits were upheld in Penn Central because they regulate use without physically occupying the property.

questions.q: An auto repair shop operated legally for 20 years. The town then rezoned the block residential, but the shop may keep operating. The shop is a:
c: Special use permit
Spot zone
Use variance
Nonconforming use
questions.x: A lawful use that predates a new restriction continues as a nonconforming (grandfathered) use. A use variance would be a new permission from the ZBA, which the shop never needed.

questions.q: In New York, practical difficulty is the standard a ZBA applies when deciding a(n):
c: Area variance
Use variance
Special use permit
Spot rezoning
questions.x: Practical difficulty, weighed through a balancing test, governs area variances. Use variances require the tougher unnecessary hardship showing on four prongs.

questions.q: An owner seeks a use variance to run an office in a residential zone. She proves no reasonable return, a unique hardship, and no harm to neighborhood character. She bought the house knowing the zoning. The likely result is:
c: Granted, since three of four prongs are met
Granted, since knowledge of zoning is irrelevant
Denied, since the hardship is self-created
Denied, since offices need a special permit
questions.x: All four prongs are required, and buying with knowledge of the restriction makes the hardship self-created, which is fatal to a use variance. 'Three of four' is the trap: the test is not a balancing test.

questions.q: For which type of zoning relief in New York is a self-created hardship fatal to the application?
c: An area variance
A special use permit
A use variance
A site plan approval
questions.x: Self-created hardship bars a use variance. For an area variance it is only one factor in the balancing test, so it does not defeat the request by itself.

questions.q: In a district of single-family homes, the town rezones one owner's half-acre lot to allow a gas station, citing no plan and no public benefit. A court is likely to find:
c: Valid incentive zoning
A valid floating zone
A valid cluster plan
Invalid spot zoning
questions.x: Singling out one parcel for a use inconsistent with its surroundings and the plan is spot zoning, generally invalid. A floating zone is a pre-approved district later mapped to land that meets its criteria, which did not happen here.

questions.q: Under incentive zoning, a developer typically receives extra height or density in exchange for:
c: Paying a higher property tax rate
Proving unnecessary hardship
Giving public amenities or benefits
Grouping homes to save open space
questions.x: Incentive zoning trades bonus density or height for public benefits such as plazas or affordable units. Grouping homes to save open space describes cluster zoning, which adds no density.

questions.q: A 60-acre tract allows one home per 3 acres. A cluster plan puts every home on a 1-acre lot and preserves the rest. Ignoring roads, how many homes are built and how many acres stay open?
c: 60 homes, 0 acres open
20 homes, 20 acres open
20 homes, 40 acres open
30 homes, 30 acres open
questions.x: Density is unchanged: 60 / 3 = 20 homes. Lots use 20 x 1 = 20 acres, leaving 60 - 20 = 40 open. '20 acres open' mistakes the lot area for the open space.

questions.q: Each of the following is usually an accessory use to a single-family home EXCEPT:
c: A detached garage
A backyard toolshed
A private swimming pool
A second, separate house
questions.x: Accessory uses are customary and incidental to the main use. A second dwelling is a principal use in its own right; a pool can seem like more than incidental, but it is a standard accessory use.

questions.q: A neighbor wants a court to overturn a planning board's site plan approval in a New York town. She should bring a(n):
c: Article 78 proceeding
Appeal to the town zoning board
Complaint to the Department of State
Request for a SEQRA declaration
questions.x: Article 78 is the court route to review local board decisions, with short filing deadlines. The ZBA hears appeals from the building inspector, not from the planning board's site plan decisions.

questions.q: In a New York town, the power to amend the zoning ordinance and zoning map belongs to the:
c: Zoning board of appeals
Planning board
Town board
Building inspector
questions.x: Zoning is legislation, so the town board (or village board or city council) adopts and amends it. The ZBA is quasi-judicial: it grants variances and interprets the ordinance but cannot rewrite it.

questions.concept: NYC Board of Standards and Appeals
questions.q: A Queens owner needs a variance to build closer to the rear lot line than zoning allows. The owner applies to the:
c: City Planning Commission
Queens Borough President
Landmarks Preservation Commission
Board of Standards and Appeals
questions.x: The BSA is NYC's zoning board of appeals and decides variances. The City Planning Commission handles zoning text and map changes through ULURP, not individual variances.

questions.q: Under New York City's ULURP, which body reviews an application first and gives a non-binding recommendation?
c: The City Council
The Community Board
The City Planning Commission
The Board of Standards and Appeals
questions.x: After certification, the Community Board has 60 days to hold a hearing and make an advisory recommendation, followed by the Borough President. The CPC's vote is binding and comes third.

questions.q: A transfer of development rights lets an owner:
c: Sell unused floor area for use on another site
Build on the lot of a neighbor who consents
Convert a nonconforming use into a legal one
Avoid property taxes on the unused air space
questions.x: A TDR moves unbuilt floor area from a sending site, such as a landmark, to a receiving site. Building on a neighbor's lot describes an easement or lease, not a transfer of development rights.

questions.q: A nonconforming machine shop in a residential zone burns down completely. Under a typical ordinance, the owner:
c: May rebuild larger, as the use is grandfathered
May rebuild once the neighbors consent in writing
May lose the right to resume the nonconforming use
Is owed compensation by the town for the lost use
questions.x: Ordinances commonly end a nonconforming use that is destroyed or abandoned, and they bar enlarging it. The grandfathered choice overreads the protection, which covers the existing use only.

questions.q: An owner's planned deck would sit 6 feet from the side lot line, but zoning requires 10 feet. To build it, the owner should seek:
c: A use variance
A rezoning
A special use permit
An area variance
questions.x: Relief from a dimensional rule such as a setback is an area variance. A use variance is for a use the district does not allow, and a deck is a permitted residential use.

questions.q: A village wants to block a state-licensed group home for adults with developmental disabilities. Under the Padavan Law, its strongest ground for objection is that:
c: The residents are not related by blood
The area already has many such homes
Property values may decline nearby
Neighbors signed a petition against it
questions.x: Padavan limits municipal objections mainly to oversaturation of the area. Arguing that residents are not related fails because towns cannot exclude these homes through a narrow definition of family.

questions.q: A zoning code lists houses of worship as allowed in a residential district if they meet parking and buffer conditions. A congregation meeting those conditions should apply for a:
c: Use variance
Nonconforming use
Rezoning
Special use permit
questions.x: When the ordinance itself allows a use subject to conditions, the owner seeks a special use permit. A use variance is for uses the ordinance does not allow, so the hardship test does not apply here.

questions.q: A use that existed lawfully before a zoning ordinance prohibited it, and is allowed to continue, is a:
c: Use variance
Special use permit
Nonconforming use
Accessory use
questions.x: A nonconforming use is grandfathered because it predates the restriction. A use variance is the trap: it is a later grant of permission by the ZBA, not protection for a pre-existing use.

questions.q: To obtain a use variance in New York, the applicant must show:
c: Practical difficulty
Unnecessary hardship
Customary incidental use
Written neighbor consent
questions.x: Use variances require unnecessary hardship, proved on all four statutory prongs. Practical difficulty is the area variance standard, the most common mix-up.

questions.q: To win a use variance, a New York applicant must prove each of the following EXCEPT:
c: No reasonable return under any permitted use
The hardship is unique to the property itself
The applicant has owned it for 10 years
The hardship was not self-created
questions.x: There is no ownership period requirement. The four prongs are no reasonable return, uniqueness, no change to neighborhood character, and not self-created; the 10-year number borrows from adverse possession.

questions.q: An owner bought a lot knowing it was 10 feet too narrow for the zoning minimum and now seeks permission to build a house. How does the self-created hardship affect the application?
c: It bars the area variance outright
It is irrelevant to the ZBA's decision
It turns the request into a use variance
It is a factor, not an automatic bar
questions.x: For area variances, self-created difficulty is one factor in the balancing test, not a bar. The 'bars it outright' choice states the use variance rule, where self-created hardship is fatal.

questions.q: Rezoning one small parcel for the benefit of its owner, inconsistent with the surrounding area and the comprehensive plan, is:
c: Spot zoning
Cluster zoning
Incentive zoning
Conditional zoning
questions.x: Spot zoning singles out a parcel for special treatment without a planning basis and is generally invalid. Conditional zoning also rezones one parcel, but it imposes conditions to protect neighbors and can be valid when consistent with the plan.

questions.q: A developer may build 4 extra stories if the project includes a public plaza and affordable units. This is:
c: Planned unit development
Incentive zoning
Spot zoning
A use variance
questions.x: Incentive zoning trades bonus density or height for public benefits. Cluster zoning keeps overall density the same while grouping homes to preserve open space, so it grants no bonus.

questions.q: A 40-acre tract is zoned for one home per 2 acres. Using cluster zoning, homes are placed on half-acre lots with the remaining land preserved. How many homes may be built, and how many acres stay open (ignoring roads)?
c: 20 homes, 30 acres open
80 homes, no acres left open
40 homes, 20 acres open
20 homes, 10 acres open
questions.x: Density stays the same: 40 / 2 = 20 homes. 20 x 0.5 = 10 acres of lots, leaving 40 - 10 = 30 acres open. The '10 acres open' choice confuses the land in lots with the land preserved.

questions.q: A detached garage on the same lot as a single-family house is an example of a(n):
c: Nonconforming use
Home occupation
Accessory use
Special use
questions.x: An accessory use is customary and incidental to the principal use on the same lot. A home occupation is a business run inside the dwelling, a different kind of secondary use.

questions.q: A person aggrieved by a New York town zoning board of appeals decision generally challenges it by:
c: An appeal to the Department of State
An Article 78 proceeding in court
A petition to the town planning board
A complaint filed with the town board
questions.x: Article 78 is the route to court review of local board decisions, generally within 30 days of the decision's filing. Neither the planning board nor the town board has appellate power over the ZBA.

questions.q: A New York zoning board of appeals may do each of the following EXCEPT:
c: Grant area variances
Interpret the zoning ordinance
Hear appeals from the building inspector
Adopt a new zoning ordinance
questions.x: The ZBA is quasi-judicial, not legislative. The town board, village board, or city council adopts and amends zoning; hearing appeals from the building inspector is a core ZBA job.

questions.concept: NYC Board of Standards and Appeals
questions.q: In New York City, applications for zoning variances are decided by the:
c: Board of Standards and Appeals
City Planning Commission
Local Community Board
Department of Buildings
questions.x: The BSA serves as NYC's zoning board of appeals. The City Planning Commission handles zoning map and text changes through ULURP, and Community Boards only advise.

questions.q: Under ULURP in New York City, which body holds a public hearing and gives a binding vote after the Community Board and Borough President have made their advisory recommendations?
c: Board of Standards and Appeals
City Planning Commission
Department of City Planning
Landmarks Preservation Commission
questions.x: The CPC has 60 days to hear and vote after the 60-day Community Board and 30-day Borough President stages; the City Council and mayor follow for many actions. The Department of City Planning is the staff agency that certifies applications, not the voting body.

questions.q: A Midtown landmark church cannot use its unused floor area because of its landmark status. It sells that floor area to a developer on a nearby receiving site. This is a:
c: Use variance for the receiving site
Special permit for bonus floor area
Transfer of development rights
Condemnation of the church's air rights
questions.x: Moving unused development rights from one site to another is a TDR. Penn Central's Grand Central air rights are the textbook example; no variance is involved because the receiving site uses rights the code already allocates.

questions.q: A deli has operated as a nonconforming use in a residential zone. The owner wants to double its size into the rear yard. Typically:
c: Expansion is allowed because the use is grandfathered
Expansion needs a building permit and nothing more
The town owes compensation if it refuses the expansion
Expansion is generally barred without ZBA relief
questions.x: Nonconforming uses may usually continue but not expand. The 'grandfathered' trap overreads the protection: it covers the existing use, not growth.

questions.q: The minimum distance a building must be set back from the front, side and rear lot lines is the zoning ordinance's:
c: Side-yard easement
Setback requirement
Right-of-way
Floor area ratio limit
questions.x: Setbacks are dimensional zoning rules, and relief from one is an area variance. Lot coverage ratio is also dimensional, but it limits the percentage of the lot a building covers, not its distance from lot lines.

questions.q: Under New York's Padavan Law, when a state-licensed operator proposes a community residence for people with developmental disabilities, the municipality may:
c: Exclude it by defining family narrowly
Object within 40 days, chiefly on oversaturation
Require the operator to win a use variance
Put the site to a vote of nearby residents
questions.x: The Padavan Law gives the municipality 40 days to suggest alternatives or object, largely limited to oversaturation of the area. Towns cannot exclude such homes through a narrow definition of family, and no variance is needed.

questions.q: A use the zoning ordinance permits in a district only if specific conditions set out in the ordinance are met requires a:
c: Use variance from the ZBA
Zoning map amendment
Special use permit
Area variance
questions.x: Special use permits (special exceptions) cover uses the ordinance contemplates subject to conditions. A use variance is for a use the ordinance does not allow at all in that district.

questions.q: An owner wants to split 20 acres into eight lots that each meet the zoning minimum. In a New York town, who approves the split?
c: The planning board, through plat review
The building inspector, by issuing permits
The zoning board of appeals, by variance
The town assessor, by new tax map lots
questions.x: Subdividing land requires planning board approval of a plat even when every lot meets the zoning. The trap is the building inspector: permits come later, for houses on approved lots. The ZBA grants relief from zoning rules, not subdivision approval.

questions.q: Which document does a planning board review and approve when land is divided into building lots?
c: The certificate of occupancy
The zoning map amendment
The subdivision plat
The tax certiorari petition
questions.x: A plat is the map of the subdivision showing lots, streets, easements and drainage, approved by the planning board and filed with the county clerk. The trap is the zoning map amendment, a legislative act by the town board that changes districts rather than dividing land.

questions.q: A lead agency concludes a proposed project may have a significant adverse environmental impact. It must:
c: Issue a negative declaration with conditions
Issue a positive declaration; require an EIS
Classify the project as a Type II action
Send the project to the state DEC to decide
questions.x: A finding that the action may have a significant adverse impact is a positive declaration, which requires an environmental impact statement with a draft, public comment, a final EIS and findings. The trap is a conditioned negative declaration, which is used for some unlisted actions but cannot replace an EIS when significant impacts are likely.

questions.q: Under SEQRA, the agency that coordinates the environmental review when several agencies must approve a project is the:
c: County planning agency
Involved agency
Interested agency
Lead agency
questions.x: When more than one agency has approval power, one becomes the lead agency and coordinates the review and determination of significance. The trap is 'involved agency', the term for each agency with approval power over the action, of which the lead is one.

questions.q: A conventional subdivision of a parcel would yield 24 lots. The planning board approves a cluster layout. The maximum number of lots is generally:
questions.x: Under Town Law 278, cluster development cannot exceed the number of lots a conventional plat would allow. It rearranges the same density onto smaller lots to preserve open space. The trap is a higher number, which describes incentive zoning, where density bonuses are traded for public benefits.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of clustering homes in a subdivision?
c: To add homes in exchange for affordable units
To permit commercial uses within a residential area
To preserve open space at the same overall density
To reduce the developer's parkland fee to zero
questions.x: Clustering puts homes on smaller lots grouped together so the rest of the land stays open, without increasing total density. The trap is adding homes for a public benefit, which is incentive zoning. Mixing in commercial uses describes a planned unit development.

questions.q: A planning board finds a town needs recreation land, but no suitable park site exists on a proposed residential plat. Under the Town Law, the board may require:
c: A money payment in lieu of parkland
A larger minimum lot size on every lot
A use variance for a future park site
A moratorium on new subdivisions
questions.x: Town Law 277 lets the board accept a payment in lieu of parkland, set by the town board and held in a recreation trust fund, when a proper park cannot be located on the plat. The trap is the moratorium, a separate legislative tool unrelated to individual plats.

questions.q: A planning board demands a parkland fee on a 10-lot plat without making any finding about the town's recreation needs. The developer's best argument is:
c: Parkland fees apply just to commercial plats
The board skipped the required finding of need
The fee is owed to the county, not the town
The plat qualifies as a cluster, which is exempt
questions.x: Before requiring parkland or a fee, the board must find that a proper case exists, based on present and future recreation needs and the population the plat will add. Without that finding the requirement is vulnerable. The trap is the commercial answer, which reverses the rule: parkland applies to residential plats.

questions.q: Four of a seven-member zoning board meet privately at a restaurant to discuss a pending variance, but take no vote. This gathering:
c: Is lawful, since no formal action was taken
Is a meeting that had to be open
Is lawful, because three members stayed away
Is a meeting if the applicant also attended
questions.x: Four of seven is a quorum, and a planned gathering of a quorum to discuss public business is a meeting under the Open Meetings Law, requiring notice and public access. The trap is 'no vote taken': deliberation counts, not just voting.

questions.q: New York's Open Meetings Law requires public bodies such as planning boards to:
c: Allow any resident to vote on land use decisions
Approve every application filed within 62 days
Record every meeting on video for the county clerk
Meet in public with advance notice
questions.x: The Open Meetings Law, the Sunshine Law, requires public bodies to meet in the open with advance notice and keep minutes; limited executive sessions are allowed for listed purposes. The trap is the 62-day answer, a subdivision deadline from the Town Law.

questions.q: After a planning board signs a final subdivision plat in a New York town, the owner must file it with the county clerk within:
c: 62 days
30 days
90 days
180 days
questions.x: Town Law 276 requires filing within 62 days of signing, or the approval expires. The trap is 180 days, the period to satisfy conditions on a conditional final approval. Thirty days is the Article 78 deadline.

questions.q: A developer received final plat approval but did not file the plat with the county clerk for four months. What is the likely status of the approval?
c: Still valid, since approvals run with the land
Valid for two years before it needs renewal
Expired, because the filing deadline passed
Converted to a preliminary approval by law
questions.x: An approved final plat must be filed within 62 days of the board's signature, or the approval expires and the developer must seek approval again. The trap is 'runs with the land', true of variances but not of an unfiled plat approval.

questions.q: A town's code lists day care centers as allowed in residential districts if the planning board finds parking and drop-off adequate. An operator needs:
c: A use variance from the zoning board of appeals
An area variance for the extra traffic it will create
A special use permit showing the conditions are met
A rezoning of the lot to a commercial district
questions.x: A use the code allows subject to conditions needs a special use permit; the applicant shows it meets the standards, not hardship. The trap is the use variance, which is for a use the district prohibits.

questions.q: How does a special use permit differ from a use variance?
c: A permit requires proof of unnecessary hardship
A permit is for a use allowed with conditions
A permit is granted by the state, not the town
A permit expires when the property is sold
questions.x: A special use permit is for a use the legislative body has already found appropriate in the district if conditions are met. A use variance permits a prohibited use and requires unnecessary hardship, which is the trap in the hardship answer. Both are local approvals.

questions.q: An owner who built a shed 3 feet into a required rear yard without a permit asks the ZBA for an area variance. The board:
c: Has to deny because the owner caused the problem
Grants it automatically if the shed is under 200 sq ft
Grants it if the owner shows no reasonable return
Weighs benefit against detriment using five factors
questions.x: Area variances use a balancing test: benefit to the applicant against detriment to the neighborhood, considering five factors. Self-created difficulty is one factor but does not bar relief. The trap is the mandatory denial, which is the use variance rule. Reasonable return is a use variance element.

questions.q: In deciding an area variance in New York, a ZBA considers all of the following EXCEPT:
c: Whether the requested variance is substantial
Whether the benefit can be achieved another way
Whether the difficulty was self-created
Whether a reasonable return is possible
questions.x: The five area variance factors are undesirable change to the neighborhood, other feasible means, substantiality, adverse physical or environmental effects, and self-creation. Reasonable return belongs to the use variance test. The trap is self-creation, which many think applies only to use variances.

questions.q: A legal nonconforming auto repair shop in a residential zone closes for 15 months. The ordinance ends nonconforming uses discontinued for one year. A buyer who wants to reopen it:
c: May reopen, since nonconforming rights pass to buyers
May reopen if it is the same type of business
Has lost the nonconforming right and needs relief
May reopen after paying a reinstatement fee
questions.x: Nonconforming rights run with the land, but they end when the use is discontinued for the period the ordinance sets. After 15 months, the right is lost; reopening would need a use variance or a rezoning. The trap is 'rights pass to buyers', true only while the use is kept alive.

questions.q: A legal nonconforming use typically may NOT be:
c: Expanded into a larger building
Sold along with the property it is on
Continued by a new owner after a sale
Mortgaged as part of the property
questions.x: A nonconforming use may usually continue and pass to a buyer, but it generally cannot be enlarged or expanded. The trap is continuation by a new owner: the right runs with the land, not with the person.

questions.q: A buyer pays a commercial price for a lot zoned residential, then seeks a use variance because a house would not earn a reasonable return on what she paid. The ZBA will most likely:
c: Grant it, since she proved no reasonable return
Deny it, since her hardship is self-created
Grant it with conditions on hours and parking
Treat it as an area variance and balance the factors
questions.x: A buyer who pays a price based on a use the zoning does not allow creates her own hardship, which bars a use variance. Reasonable return is also measured against a reasonable price, not an inflated one. The trap is the balancing answer, which applies to area variances.

questions.q: For a use variance in New York, the applicant must show unnecessary hardship, which includes all of these EXCEPT:
c: No reasonable return under any permitted use
A larger profit from the proposed new use
Hardship unique to the property
Hardship that was not self-created
questions.x: The four elements are no reasonable return under permitted uses (with dollars and cents proof), uniqueness, no change to neighborhood character, and no self-creation. A bigger profit from the new use is not hardship. The trap is uniqueness, which some forget is required.

questions.q: A village ZBA grants a variance, and the decision is filed with the village clerk on May 1. A neighbor who wants to challenge it should file an Article 78 proceeding by about:
c: May 1 of next year
June 30
August 29
May 31
questions.x: Challenges to a village or town ZBA decision must be brought within 30 days after the decision is filed with the clerk, so about May 31. The trap is August 29, about four months, the general Article 78 limit that the zoning statutes shorten.

questions.q: In New York, an owner aggrieved by a zoning board of appeals decision seeks court review through:
c: An Article 78 proceeding
A tax certiorari petition
A small claims case
A quiet title action
questions.x: An Article 78 proceeding in State Supreme Court reviews whether the board acted illegally, arbitrarily, or without substantial evidence. The trap is tax certiorari, which challenges property tax assessments, not zoning decisions.

questions.q: A state-licensed community residence for adults with disabilities is proposed in a single-family zone. Under the Padavan Law, the town's main grounds to object are:
c: Lower property values and increased traffic
Lack of a use variance from the town's ZBA
Oversaturation or changed area character
Neighbors' safety concerns about the residents
questions.x: The Padavan Law gives the municipality 40 days to suggest alternatives or object, essentially on oversaturation of similar facilities or a substantial change in the area's character. The trap is safety fears about residents, which are discriminatory and not a lawful ground. No use variance is required.

questions.q: A village code limits single-family homes to people related by blood, marriage, or adoption. Four unrelated adults share a house, meals, and expenses on a long lease. Under New York law:
c: The code may be enforced, since it is clear and neutral
The code applies unless one of them owns the home
It cannot exclude them if they function as a family
The code may be enforced if the village pays relocation
questions.x: New York's Court of Appeals has held that a zoning definition based solely on biological or legal relationship cannot exclude unrelated people living as the functional equivalent of a family. The trap is the neutrality argument: a clearly written rule can still be unconstitutional as applied.

questions.q: A NYC lot is 25 feet by 100 feet in a district with a maximum FAR of 3.0. The existing building has 5,500 square feet of zoning floor area. How much unused floor area remains?
c: 7,500 square feet
2,000 square feet
5,500 square feet
12,500 square feet
questions.x: Lot area = 2,500 square feet. Maximum floor area = 2,500 x 3.0 = 7,500. Unused = 7,500 minus 5,500 = 2,000 square feet. The trap is 7,500, the total allowed rather than what remains. 12,500 multiplies the lot area by 5 instead of the 3.0 FAR.

questions.q: In New York City zoning, 'air rights' most precisely refers to:
c: The airspace above a building's roof line
Light and air guaranteed to neighbors
The FAA's control of flight paths
Unused zoning floor area on a lot
questions.x: Air rights are the unused development rights on a zoning lot: the difference between the maximum floor area the zoning allows and the floor area built. The trap is the literal airspace answer; what is sold is floor area, which can be used on the lot or moved under the zoning rules.

questions.q: An owner in a NYC historic district wants to remove a 19th-century stoop and cornice from her facade. She needs:
c: A Certificate of No Effect from LPC staff
A BSA variance under the five findings
A Permit for Minor Work from LPC staff
A Certificate of Appropriateness
questions.x: Removing significant architectural features such as a stoop or cornice is a major change needing a Certificate of Appropriateness, voted by the Commission after a public hearing. The trap is the Permit for Minor Work, which covers routine work like restoring windows or masonry repair. The BSA handles zoning, not landmarks.

questions.q: A Certificate of No Effect from the Landmarks Preservation Commission is typically issued for:
c: A visible rooftop addition on a rowhouse
Demolition of a building in a district
Interior work needing a DOB permit only
Rezoning of a block in a historic district
questions.x: A Certificate of No Effect covers work that requires a Department of Buildings permit but does not affect the building's protected features, such as many interior renovations. The trap is the rooftop addition, which typically needs a Certificate of Appropriateness after a hearing.

questions.q: A city's landmark law bars an owner from building a tower over a designated train station, but the station still operates profitably and its development rights can be transferred. Under Penn Central, this is:
c: Not a taking, since a reasonable return remains
A taking, because the tower would be worth millions
A taking, because designation is a physical occupation
Not a taking, since landmarks are exempt from takings
questions.x: Penn Central held that landmark restrictions leaving the owner a reasonable return, with transferable development rights, are not a taking. The trap is the physical occupation answer: Loretto makes permanent physical occupations takings, but a use restriction is not an occupation.

questions.q: Which situation is the clearest taking that requires just compensation?
c: A landmark designation that blocks a taller building
A law requiring a cable box bolted to a roof
A zoning change that lowers the allowed building height
A temporary moratorium while a plan is updated
questions.x: Under Loretto v. Teleprompter, any permanent physical occupation authorized by government is a taking, however small. The trap is the landmark designation, which Penn Central held is not a taking when the owner keeps a reasonable use and return.

questions.concept: Zoning lot merger vs landmark transfer
questions.q: Two adjacent NYC lot owners, neither a landmark, want to shift 1,000 square feet of unused floor area from one lot to the other. The usual method is:
c: A ZR 74-79 special permit through ULURP
A zoning lot merger, generally as of right
A BSA area variance for the receiving lot
A rezoning of both lots by the City Council
questions.x: Adjacent lots can merge into a single zoning lot, with recorded documents, and floor area can then be used anywhere on the merged lot. No public review is generally needed. The trap is the ZR 74-79 special permit, which is the landmark transfer route, not the ordinary adjacent merger.

questions.concept: Zoning lot merger vs landmark transfer
questions.q: A designated landmark theater wants to sell development rights to a site across the street. The approval it needs is:
c: A zoning lot merger recorded with ACRIS, with no review
A Certificate of No Effect from the LPC staff
A BSA variance with the five required findings
A CPC special permit under ZR 74-79, through ULURP
questions.x: ZR 74-79 lets a landmark transfer unused development rights to an adjacent, across-the-street, or same-corner lot by City Planning Commission special permit, which goes through ULURP. The trap is the zoning lot merger, which requires lots that are actually adjacent and merged.

questions.q: In ULURP, which body's vote on a zoning map change is advisory only?
c: The community board
The City Council
The City Planning Commission
The Board of Standards and Appeals
questions.x: Community boards and borough presidents give advisory recommendations. The CPC and the City Council take binding votes on zoning map changes. The trap is the BSA, which is not part of ULURP at all; it hears variances and certain special permits.

questions.q: In ULURP, the community board has how long to hold a hearing and make its recommendation after certification?
c: 30 days
50 days
60 days
120 days
questions.x: The community board has 60 days. Then the borough president has 30, the CPC 60, the City Council 50, and the mayor 5. The trap is 30 days, the borough president's period. 120 days is not a ULURP step.

questions.q: Which body grants a use variance for a lot in New York City, and on what standard?
c: The CPC, by special permit after ULURP review
The LPC, after a Certificate of Appropriateness
The BSA, after making five required findings
A local ZBA, using the Town Law's four elements
questions.x: In NYC, the Board of Standards and Appeals grants variances, making five findings under ZR 72-21, including unique physical conditions and minimum variance. The trap is the CPC, which grants its own special permits and votes on rezonings but does not grant variances.

questions.q: The BSA must find all of the following to grant a variance EXCEPT that:
c: The community board voted in favor of it
The variance is the minimum needed for relief
Unique physical conditions create a hardship
The hardship was not created by the owner
questions.x: The five findings are unique physical conditions, no reasonable return, no change to neighborhood character, no owner-created hardship, and minimum variance. A community board recommendation is advisory, not a required finding. The trap is the minimum variance finding, which candidates who know only the town test miss.

questions.q: A Dutchess County village publishes its determination and findings to condemn a vacant lot for a firehouse. The owner argues the taking serves no public use. She should file:
c: An Article 78 petition in State Supreme Court within four months of the decision
A petition in the Appellate Division within 30 days after publication
A claim in the Court of Claims within 3 years after title vests
An appeal to the village zoning board of appeals within 60 days
questions.x: EDPL 207 sends a challenge to the condemnor's determination and findings to the Appellate Division for the department where the property is, within 30 days after publication is complete. The Article 78 choice is the trap: it is the normal route for agency decisions, but the EDPL has its own shorter path. The 3-year claim is for compensation, not for contesting the taking itself.

questions.q: Under New York's Eminent Domain Procedure Law, a court reviewing a condemnor's determination to take property considers whether:
c: The owner received the highest price an appraiser would support
The taking is the least costly way to build the planned project
A public use is served and the required procedures were followed
The town's zoning permits the project on the property to be taken
questions.x: EDPL 207 limits the Appellate Division's review to constitutional issues, the condemnor's authority, compliance with the EDPL and SEQRA procedures, and whether a public use, benefit, or purpose is served. The price choice is the trap: compensation is decided later in a separate claim, so the amount offered is not an issue in the challenge to the taking.

questions.q: The State takes a 4,000 square foot strip of a gas station lot for a road project. The whole lot was worth $900,000 before the taking; the remainder is worth $780,000 after it. The strip alone is worth $60,000. Under the usual New York measure, just compensation is about:
questions.x: For a partial taking, courts generally use the before-and-after measure: $900,000 minus $780,000 is $120,000. That covers the $60,000 strip plus $60,000 of consequential damage to the remainder. The $60,000 choice is the trap: paying for the strip alone ignores the harm to what the owner keeps. Adding the strip value to the difference ($180,000) would count the strip twice.

questions.q: A county takes the front 30 feet of a shopping center lot, eliminating 40 parking spaces. In addition to the value of the land taken, the owner may recover for:
c: Consequential damage that lowers the value of the remaining property
The tenants' lost sales, paid directly to each tenant by the county
The owner's income taxes on the award, which the county has to gross up
Nothing more, since compensation is limited to the land actually taken
questions.x: Just compensation for a partial taking includes direct damages for the land taken and consequential damages that reduce the value of the remainder, such as lost parking, proven with expert evidence. The before-and-after comparison captures both. The 'land taken only' choice is the trap: it would leave the owner bearing a loss the Constitution requires the public to pay.

questions.q: A manufacturer in Oneida County builds a plant under an industrial development agency PILOT agreement. Its tax bill lists county, town, and school taxes, a water district levy, and a curb special assessment. The IDA exemption removes:
c: Every item, replaced by a single PILOT payment to the IDA
The water district levy and the curb assessment, which help fund the IDA
The school tax alone, since the town and county share the PILOT
The county, town, and school general taxes, replaced by the PILOT
questions.x: An IDA exemption under General Municipal Law 874 covers general taxes levied by counties, cities, towns, villages, and school districts, and the PILOT agreement substitutes negotiated payments for them. It does not cover special ad valorem levies such as district charges, or special assessments. The 'every item' choice is the trap: special district and assessment charges keep coming.

questions.q: A property in an industrial development agency PILOT program is exempt from all of the following EXCEPT:
c: The county general tax
The school district tax
A sewer district levy
The town general tax
questions.x: The IDA exemption reaches general taxes of counties, towns, cities, villages, and school districts, which the PILOT replaces. A sewer district levy is a special ad valorem levy charged to parcels inside the district, and special levies and special assessments stay on the bill. The school tax is the tempting wrong pick because some PILOTs share payments unevenly, but it is still a general tax covered by the exemption.

questions.q: A town planning board reviewing a site plan for a car wash on Route 17 may lawfully attach which condition?
c: A gift of land for a new town hall across town
A cap on the prices the car wash may charge
Screening and lighting limits facing nearby homes
A requirement that the owner hire town residents
questions.x: Town Law 274-a allows reasonable conditions that are directly related and incidental to the proposed site plan, such as screening, lighting, and access. They must be met before permits issue. A town hall land gift, price controls, and hiring rules have no connection to the site's layout. The land gift is the tempting trap because boards may require parkland in subdivisions, but that is a separate rule with its own findings.

questions.q: A site plan for a permitted medical office in a Saratoga County town shows a 20-foot front setback where zoning requires 35. The applicant may:
c: Seek a use variance from the ZBA, after the planning board rejects the plan
Wait for a building permit denial, then appeal it to the planning board
Ask the planning board to waive the setback as part of its site plan approval
Apply directly to the ZBA for an area variance, without a prior denial
questions.x: Town Law 274-a lets an applicant whose site plan contains a feature that does not comply with zoning go straight to the zoning board of appeals for an area variance, without first being denied by the enforcement officer. A setback is dimensional, so a use variance is the trap: the medical office use is permitted. A planning board reviews layout and cannot vary the setback.

questions.q: In a New York town, a planned unit development district mixing townhouses, shops, and open space is created by:
c: The town board, by amending the zoning law
The planning board, by approving a subdivision
The zoning board of appeals, by a use variance
The county, through its planning referral
questions.x: Town Law 261-c authorizes the town's legislative body to provide for planned unit development districts in its zoning law, so creating and mapping one is a legislative rezoning by the town board. The planning board typically reviews the detailed plans afterward. The use variance choice is the trap: a ZBA can relieve a hardship on one parcel but cannot create a new district.

questions.q: Neighbors want to stop a proposed 200-unit planned unit development on land zoned for one-acre lots in a Westchester town. Their most direct audience is:
c: The zoning board of appeals, which grants PUDs
The town board, which must adopt the PUD district
The building inspector, who issues the PUD permit
The county clerk, who records the approved PUD map
questions.x: A PUD district is created by the town's legislative body as an amendment to the zoning law, after a public hearing, so the town board's vote is the decision that matters. The ZBA choice is the trap: variances are for hardship on a single parcel, while a PUD is a rezoning. The building inspector and county clerk act only after approvals exist.

questions.q: A Long Island town's building inspector finds a contractor framing an addition with no building permit. Under New York's Uniform Code enforcement rules, the inspector may issue:
c: A use variance denial, which the owner may appeal to the ZBA
A stop work order stating the reason and the conditions to resume
A certificate of noncompliance that voids the house's existing CO
A demolition order, effective at once, for the unpermitted framing
questions.x: Local code enforcement programs must provide for stop work orders when work proceeds without a required permit, is unsafe, or violates the code. The order states why it was issued and what must happen before work may resume, usually getting the permit and passing inspection. The demolition choice is the trap: removing work is a remedy for unsafe conditions, not the first step for a missing permit.

questions.q: Under New York's minimum code enforcement standards, a building containing a restaurant that seats 120 people must receive fire safety inspections at least every:
c: Year
Two years
Three years
Five years
questions.x: Buildings with an assembly area, a space for 50 or more people such as a restaurant dining room, must be inspected at intervals of no more than one year, and they need an operating permit. Three years is the trap: it is the maximum interval for multiple dwellings and other nonresidential occupancies, which would apply if the building had no assembly area.

cram.html: Government powers = PETE: Police power, Eminent domain, Taxation, Escheat. Only eminent domain pays.
Zoning, building codes, subdivision rules = police power. No compensation.
Eminent domain needs public use + just compensation; the process is condemnation (NY: Eminent Domain Procedure Law).
Public vs private control conflict: the more restrictive one governs. A variance does not cancel a covenant.
Zoning is adopted by the legislative body (town board, village trustees, city council) in accordance with the comprehensive plan.
Planning board: master plan, official map, subdivisions (plat), site plans, PUDs, clustering. ZBA: variances, interpretations, appeals, often special permits.
Use variance = unnecessary hardship, all 4: no reasonable return, unique, won't change character, not self-created.
Area variance = practical difficulty, 5-factor balancing; self-created counts but does not bar it.
Nonconforming use: predates zoning, may continue, cannot expand, lost if abandoned. Illegal uses are never grandfathered.
Special use permit = listed use with conditions. Use variance = use the code does not allow.
Clustering keeps density the same (acres / min lot size = homes). Incentive zoning adds density for a public benefit.
Spot zoning: one parcel, one owner benefits, inconsistent with the plan. Void.
Challenge a ZBA or planning board decision: Article 78, within 30 days of filing with the clerk.
SEQRA: lead agency, EAF, negative declaration (no EIS) or positive declaration (EIS). NYC version: CEQR.
Open Meetings Law: public meetings, notice at least 72 hours ahead for meetings scheduled a week out, minutes kept.
Interstate Land Sales Act: 100+ lots, property report, 7-day revocation. Now CFPB (formerly HUD).
Article 9-A: vacant subdivided land sold to NY residents on installment plans; file with Department of State.
Permit before work, CO after final inspection. CO states the legal use: check it before advertising unit counts.
NYC: variances = BSA; rezonings = CPC + City Council via ULURP (CB 60, BP 30, CPC 60, Council 50, Mayor 5).
Penn Central (1978): landmarking Grand Central not a taking. Loretto (1982): any permanent physical occupation is a taking.
Padavan Law: town gets 40 days to respond to a proposed community residence; cannot exclude via narrow family definitions.

subjects.title: Construction and Environmental Issues
subjects.blurb: You will walk buyers through basements, boilers and panels, and you are liable for what you knew about lead, radon, mold and buried oil tanks. The exam tests structural vocabulary, system basics, and every major environmental hazard and law.

lessons.title: How a House Is Built: Permits, Site, Structure, and Warranties
lessons.tagline: From footing to ridge beam: if you can name it, you can sell it, and spot when something is wrong.
objectives: Follow a project from plans and specifications through permit, inspections and CO
Explain NY's on-site well, septic, and Energy Code requirements
Name every structural member from footing to ridge and say what it carries
Explain R-value, insulation types and locations, and the building envelope
State the Housing Merchant Implied Warranty periods and home improvement contract rules

blocks.title: A new build in Saugerties
blocks.html: Leo is buying a brand-new colonial from a small builder in Ulster County. Private well, septic system, slab garage, full basement. The builder says, "CO's coming next week, and you've got my word on the warranty." Leo has a spreadsheet with 41 questions. Which ones actually matter?
blocks.casual: Leo's buying a brand-new colonial from a small builder in Ulster County. It's got a private well, a septic system, a garage on a slab, and a full basement. The builder tells him, "CO's coming next week, and you've got my word on the warranty." Leo has a spreadsheet with 41 questions. Which ones actually matter?
