Pricing the house below the appraised value
questions.x: The implied warranty can be excluded only by offering a written limited warranty that meets the statute's minimums. An oral as-is statement does not exclude it.

questions.q: A bathroom exhaust fan in a New York house should be ducted:
c: Into the attic above the bath
Into the nearest wall cavity
To the outside of the house
Into the basement crawl space
questions.x: Bath and kitchen fans must vent outside, never into the attic, where the moist air causes mold and rot. Venting into the attic is the common shortcut and the trap.

questions.q: In a well-ventilated attic, air typically enters through the ____ and leaves through the ____.
c: Ridge vents; soffit or fascia vents
Gable vents; bathroom exhaust fans
Fascia boards; chimney flue
Soffit vents; ridge or gable vents
questions.x: Air comes in low at the soffits and exits high at the ridge or gables, keeping the roof deck cold and preventing ice dams. Reversing the flow is the trap.

questions.q: New York requires carbon monoxide alarms in homes that have:
c: Fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage
Only electric heat and an electric range
Three or more rental units in the same building
A private well and a septic system
questions.x: CO alarms are required in NY homes with fuel-burning appliances or attached garages. Three or more units is a number borrowed from other housing rules.

questions.q: A buyer's home has an oil boiler, a gas water heater and an attached garage. Which statement is correct?
c: CO alarms are optional because the boiler is vented
Flues and combustion air are needed, and CO alarms are required
Only the garage requires a CO alarm, not the boiler
No CO alarm is needed as long as a working smoke detector is present
questions.x: Combustion appliances need combustion air and a proper flue, and NY requires CO alarms where there are fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage. A smoke detector does not detect carbon monoxide.

questions.q: The main difference between a boiler and a furnace is that a boiler:
c: Heats air, while a furnace heats water
Burns oil, while a furnace burns gas
Heats water, while a furnace heats air
Needs ducts, while a furnace needs pipes
questions.x: A boiler heats water (hot water or steam) for radiators or baseboards; a furnace heats air sent through ducts. Fuel type does not define either one.

questions.q: A house has baseboard fins, a circulator pump and an expansion tank, but no ductwork. A buyer wants central air. The agent should know that:
c: The furnace blower can carry the cooling
Steam radiators can be converted to cooling
The expansion tank doubles as a condenser
The hydronic system has no ducts to share
questions.x: Those are the tells of a hot water (hydronic) boiler system, which includes no AC ductwork. Only forced warm air has ducts and a blower that central air can share.

questions.q: Which heating fuel is delivered by truck and stored in a tank on the property?
c: Heating oil
Natural gas
Electric power
District steam
questions.x: Oil is stored on site and delivered by truck. Natural gas is piped by the utility with no tank, the most common confusion.

questions.q: Electric baseboard resistance heat is best described as:
c: Costly to install but cheap to run
Cheap to install but expensive to run
Efficient enough to beat a heat pump
Dependent on an on-site fuel tank and delivery
questions.x: Baseboard resistance heat costs little to install and a lot to operate; heat pumps are far more efficient. The reverse statement is the trap.

questions.q: A typical tank water heater lasts about:
c: 25 to 35 years
15 to 25 years
8 to 12 years
40 to 60 years
questions.x: Tank water heaters last roughly 8 to 12 years. Fifteen to 25 years is the furnace range, and 25 to 35 is for cast iron boilers.

questions.q: Which heating equipment usually has the longest life expectancy?
c: A forced air furnace
A tank water heater
A central AC compressor
A cast iron boiler
questions.x: Cast iron boilers commonly run 25 to 35+ years, longer than furnaces (15 to 25) or compressors (10 to 15).

questions.q: A homeowner converts from oil to gas. The old heating oil tank should be:
c: Emptied, cleaned, and removed or filled, with proof
Left in place with the fill pipe capped and no other steps
Kept partly full in case the owner switches back to oil
Registered with DEC as an active petroleum facility
questions.x: An abandoned tank should be emptied, cleaned, and removed or filled with inert material, with paperwork to prove it. Just capping the fill pipe leaves oil behind and invites a delivery into it.

questions.q: Which statement about home heating oil tanks used on the premises in New York is correct?
c: All must be registered and tested annually with DEC
Most fall below DEC's threshold, but spills must be reported
They are exempt from spill reporting because they are small home tanks
Only underground ones are covered by the Navigation Law
questions.x: Most home heating oil tanks are below the registration threshold, yet any petroleum spill must be reported to DEC within 2 hours. Being small does not exempt a tank from reporting.

questions.q: For a house on a town water main, the owner is usually responsible for the water line from the:
c: Treatment plant to the meter
Street main to the curb valve
Curb valve into the house
Meter to the street main
questions.x: The owner is usually responsible from the curb valve in. The main and the line up to the curb valve are the water utility's side.

questions.q: Each of the following is a source of domestic hot water EXCEPT:
c: A tank water heater
A tankless coil in a boiler
An indirect tank heated by a boiler
A pressure tank on a well
questions.x: Hot water comes from a tank heater, a tankless coil inside a boiler, or an indirect tank. A well's pressure tank stores cold water under pressure.

questions.q: Which pipe material is typically used for waste and vent stacks in older homes?
c: Cast iron
Copper
Galvanized steel
Brass
questions.x: Cast iron is the classic waste and vent stack material: quiet and durable, though it rusts and cracks with age. Copper and brass are supply materials.

questions.q: An inspector finds lead pipe on the water service line of an old house. The right advice is that it:
c: Is a durable supply pipe needing no action
Is a health hazard that should be replaced
Is acceptable as long as the water is slightly acidic
Only matters if the house uses a well
questions.x: Lead service lines have no acceptable use today: they are a health hazard that must be identified and replaced. Acidic water makes lead leach more, not less.

questions.q: Who typically owns the electric meter on a house?
c: The homeowner
The electrician of record
The utility company
The local building department
questions.x: The utility brings service to the property and owns the meter. The owner is responsible from the service entrance into the house.

questions.q: The landowner is responsible for the electrical system starting at the:
c: Nearest utility pole on the street
Utility's substation serving the block
First outlet inside the house
Service entrance (weatherhead or meter base)
questions.x: Everything from the service entrance into the house (service cable, panel, wiring, devices) is the owner's. The service drop or lateral up to it is the utility's.

questions.q: In an older house, asbestos is most likely to be found in:
c: Boiler and heating pipe wrap
Copper water supply lines
Fiberglass batt insulation
PVC drain, waste and vent pipes in the basement
questions.x: Asbestos was prized for fireproofing and shows up in pipe and boiler wrap, 9 by 9 inch floor tiles, texture coatings, shingles and vermiculite. Fiberglass batts are not asbestos.

questions.q: Which statement about asbestos regulation is correct?
c: EPA banned all asbestos use in residential paint in 1978
EPA banned chrysotile, the last form in use, in 2024
Asbestos has never been banned for any use in the U.S.
Asbestos was banned with PCBs in 1979
questions.x: EPA banned the last form of asbestos still in use, chrysotile, in 2024. 1978 is the residential lead paint ban and 1979 the PCB ban.

questions.q: Intact, non-friable asbestos floor tile in good condition is often best handled by:
c: Having the owner scrape it up promptly
Sanding it smooth before refinishing
Leaving it alone or encapsulating it
Removing it before any sale can close
questions.x: Intact, non-friable asbestos is often safest left alone, encapsulated or enclosed. Assuming removal is required is the trap; removal is the riskiest option.

questions.q: In New York, asbestos removal from a building must be done by contractors licensed by the:
c: NYS Department of State
Department of Environmental Conservation
County health department
NYS Department of Labor
questions.x: The NYS Department of Labor licenses asbestos contractors, and NYC DEP adds its own rules. DEC certifies pesticide applicators, a neighboring licensing rule.

questions.q: Lead-based paint was banned for residential use in:
questions.x: Residential lead paint was banned in 1978, the cutoff for the federal disclosure rule. 1979 is the PCB ban and 1988 the chlordane ban.

questions.q: Who faces the greatest harm from even low levels of lead exposure?
c: Adults over 65
Children under 6
Teenagers in school
Healthy adult renters
questions.x: Children under 6 absorb lead easily, and low levels damage the brain and nervous system. Adults face blood pressure and kidney harm, but children are most at risk.

questions.q: Under the federal lead disclosure rule, sellers and agents must keep the signed disclosure paperwork for:
c: 1 year
5 years
3 years
10 days
questions.x: Seller and agents keep the records 3 years. Ten days is the buyer's inspection window, a different number in the same rule.

questions.q: A seller of a 1950 house tells her agent she will skip the lead pamphlet and disclosure form. The agent's best course is to:
c: Let it go, since the disclosure duty belongs only to the seller
Give the pamphlet but skip the signed disclosure
Have the buyer waive the rule in the contract
Make sure the seller complies, or share the liability
questions.x: Agents must make sure sellers and landlords comply or share liability. Only the 10-day testing period can be waived; the pamphlet and disclosure cannot.

questions.q: The federal lead disclosure rule applies to each of the following leases of pre-1978 housing EXCEPT a:
c: Two-year lease of a two-bedroom unit
One-year lease of a family home
One-year lease of a three-bedroom flat
90-day lease of a furnished house
questions.x: Short-term leases of 100 days or less are exempt. The other leases run longer than 100 days on units with bedrooms, so the rule applies to them.

questions.q: Senior housing built in 1970 is exempt from the lead disclosure rule unless:
c: A child under 6 lives there
The building has 3 or more units
The lease runs over 100 days
The building has an elevator
questions.x: Housing for the elderly or disabled is exempt unless a child under 6 lives there. Three or more units is from NYC Local Law 1, not the federal exemption.

questions.q: NYC Local Law 1 of 2004 requires landlords to find and fix lead paint hazards in buildings with 3 or more units built before:
questions.x: LL1 covers 3+ unit buildings built before 1960 (or 1960 to 1978 if lead paint is known). 1978 is the federal disclosure cutoff, the tempting mix-up.

questions.q: In a 1955 Bronx walk-up with 6 units, a landlord's duty to find and fix lead paint hazards under Local Law 1 is triggered when a child under 6:
c: Is named on the lease as the tenant of record for the unit
Has an elevated blood lead test on file
Lives in the unit or spends 10+ hours a week there
Lives anywhere within the same block
questions.x: The duty applies where a child under 6 lives or regularly spends 10 or more hours a week. A positive blood test is not required first.

questions.q: Radon gas comes from:
c: Leaking fuel oil in buried tanks
Formaldehyde in foam insulation
Uranium breaking down in soil and rock
Combustion gases from a faulty furnace or boiler
questions.x: Radon forms from the natural breakdown of uranium in soil and rock. Combustion produces carbon monoxide, a different hazard.

questions.q: Radon is the leading cause of lung cancer among:
c: Smokers over 50
Children under 6
Asbestos workers
Nonsmokers
questions.x: Radon is the leading cause of lung cancer in nonsmokers. Children under 6 is the lead-risk group, a borrowed fact.

questions.q: The first step in dealing with mold in a basement is to:
c: Fix the moisture source
Paint over the stains
Run an ozone generator
Replace the furnace filter
questions.x: Mold grows where moisture persists, so the water problem is fixed first, then moldy materials are cleaned or removed. Painting over it leaves the cause in place.

questions.q: Mold in a home is most closely linked to:
c: Uranium breaking down in the soil under the slab
Persistent moisture from leaks or humidity
Aluminum wiring at the outlets
High-voltage lines near the lot
questions.x: Mold needs moisture: leaks, floods, humid basements, poorly vented baths. Uranium in soil is the radon source.

questions.q: Who is responsible for the water quality of a private household well in New York?
c: The EPA under the SDWA
The local water district
The well owner
The well driller forever
questions.x: A private well owner alone is responsible for its quality; the Safe Drinking Water Act covers public systems, not private wells.

questions.q: NYC's drinking water comes mainly from the:
c: Hudson River below Albany
Long Island aquifer wells pumped by the city
Great Lakes intake pipes
Catskill, Delaware and Croton reservoirs
questions.x: NYC's water comes from the Catskill, Delaware and Croton reservoirs. Long Island relies on its aquifer, which is the trap for downstate readers.

questions.q: A well test shows coliform bacteria. A typical first fix is:
c: Shock chlorination and repair of the well cap
A water softener installed on the main supply line
A neutralizing filter for pH
Replacing the copper supply pipes
questions.x: Bacteria are treated with shock chlorination, fixing the cap or casing, or UV treatment. Softeners treat hardness, a different problem.

questions.q: Blue-green stains on fixtures in a house with a well usually point to:
c: Hard water with calcium
Acidic water corroding copper
Iron and manganese minerals
Coliform bacteria
questions.x: Acidic (low pH) water corrodes copper, leaving blue-green stains, and can leach lead; a neutralizing filter fixes it. Iron and manganese cause rust-colored stains instead.

questions.q: In a septic system, where do solids settle and break down?
c: In the absorption field
In the vent stack
In the septic tank
In the seepage pit gravel
questions.x: Solids settle in the tank, where bacteria break them down; liquid flows on to the absorption field or seepage pits. The field filters liquid, not solids.

questions.q: In a septic system, the soil of the absorption (leach) field serves to:
c: Hold the solids until the tank is next pumped out
Supply fresh water to the well
Vent sewer gas through the roof
Filter the liquid that flows from the tank
questions.x: The tank settles solids; the field's soil filters the liquid. Holding solids is the tank's job, the most common mix-up.

questions.q: Which septic evaluation gives a buyer the most reliable picture?
c: A full inspection with pumping
A dye test flushed down the toilet
A seller's statement that it works
A review of the last tax bill
questions.x: A dye test is limited; a full inspection with pumping, tank inspection and field evaluation is better. The dye test is tempting because it is quick and common.

questions.q: A homeowner with a septic field should avoid:
c: Pumping the tank every few years
Driving or parking vehicles on the field
Keeping the as-built drawing on file
Directing gutter downspouts away from the field
questions.x: Never drive over or plant trees on the field; failed fields can cost tens of thousands to replace. Regular pumping is good practice, not a hazard.

questions.q: Under New York's Navigation Law, the person responsible for a petroleum discharge is liable for cleanup:
c: Only if negligence is proven
Only for spills over 100 gallons
Strictly, without proof of fault
Only if the tank was registered
questions.x: The Navigation Law makes the discharger strictly liable for petroleum cleanup. Requiring proof of negligence is the trap, and registration status does not matter.

questions.q: Which tanks face the heaviest federal and state rules (registration, leak detection, corrosion protection, closure reports)?
c: Residential heating oil tanks
Aboveground basement tanks
Propane grill cylinders
Commercial motor fuel tanks
questions.x: Commercial motor fuel tanks are regulated by EPA and DEC; residential heating oil tanks are lightly regulated, though a leak is still the owner's problem.

questions.q: After contaminated soil around a leaking tank is cleaned up, the owner should obtain from DEC a:
c: DEC spill closure letter
Certificate of occupancy for the tank
Phase IV monitoring permit
Tank registration certificate
questions.x: The cleanup step ends with a DEC spill closure letter stating no further action. A certificate of occupancy is a building department document, not a spill document.

questions.q: To find out whether a property has a buried tank, an inspector would most likely use a:
c: Percolation test of the soil
Tank sweep with a metal detector
Radon canister set in the basement
Gaussmeter run along the lot line
questions.x: A tank sweep (metal detection) finds buried tanks; tightness tests or soil borings then test them. A perc test measures soil absorption for septic design.

questions.q: Which federal law regulates asbestos handling during demolition and renovation?
c: Safe Drinking Water Act
CERCLA (Superfund)
Clean Air Act (NESHAP)
Clean Water Act
questions.x: The Clean Air Act, through NESHAP, regulates asbestos during demolition and renovation and also phases out CFCs. CERCLA covers cleanup of hazardous waste sites.

questions.q: The phaseout of CFC refrigerants in the U.S. is carried out under the:
c: Safe Drinking Water Act
Navigation Law
SARA amendments
Clean Air Act
questions.x: CFCs are phased out under the Montreal Protocol and the Clean Air Act. SARA amended Superfund and created the innocent landowner defense.

questions.q: On January 1, 2028, DEC's general size threshold for regulated freshwater wetlands drops from 12.4 acres to:
c: 7.4 acres
10 acres
1 acre
5.4 acres
questions.x: The threshold drops from 12.4 to 7.4 acres in 2028. Since 2025 DEC can also regulate wetlands of unusual importance regardless of size.

questions.q: Since January 1, 2025, DEC may regulate a freshwater wetland of unusual importance:
c: Only if it exceeds 12.4 acres
Regardless of its size
Only if it appears on DEC's old maps
Only if it is tidal
questions.x: DEC no longer relies only on its old maps and can regulate wetlands of unusual importance regardless of size. The 12.4-acre figure is the general threshold, not a limit on these.

questions.q: Who fills out the Property Condition Disclosure Statement for a 1 to 4 family sale?
c: The listing agent
The home inspector
The seller
The buyer's attorney
questions.x: The seller fills out the PCDS, not the agent. An agent who completes it is playing expert on facts only the seller knows.

questions.q: An agent recommends a radon test and a tank sweep to her buyer. To protect herself and the client, she should also:
c: Sign the seller's disclosure form herself
Tell the buyer the house is likely fine
Order the tests without telling the buyer
Write down what she recommended and when
questions.x: Agents should document what they recommended and when. Reassuring the buyer that the house is fine is exactly the expert opinion agents must not give.

questions.q: An inspector notes that the concrete pad under a foundation wall sits above the frost line and is cracking from heaving. Which component has the problem?
c: The sill plate
The girder
The floor joists
The footing
questions.x: Footings must sit below the frost line so freezing soil cannot lift them. The sill plate rests on top of the foundation wall, so it is above the problem, not the concrete base below it.

questions.q: In a basement, a Lally column most directly supports the:
c: Roof rafters
Footing
Girder
Window header
questions.x: Lally columns hold up the main girder, which carries the floor joists. The footing is under the column, so the column rests on it rather than supporting it.

questions.q: A termite inspector probes the first piece of wood that rests directly on the concrete foundation wall and finds it soft. The damaged member is the:
c: Sill plate
Ridge board
Top plate
Subfloor
questions.x: The sill plate is the lowest wood member, anchored to the foundation, which makes it a common spot for rot and termites. The top plate also has 'plate' in its name, but it caps the top of the wall studs.

questions.q: In a brick wall, the horizontal member that spans the top of a window opening and carries the masonry above it is a:
c: Header
Sill
Joist
Lintel
questions.x: Over openings in masonry the member is a lintel, often steel or stone. 'Header' is the wood-framing term for the same job, which makes it the trap here.

questions.q: A renovator needs a beam that carries more load without getting any deeper, so he bolts a steel plate between two 2x12s. He has built a:
c: Glulam beam
Box header
Lally beam
Flitch plate beam
questions.x: Sandwiching steel between wood boards makes a flitch plate beam. A glulam beam is also engineered, but it is made of glued wood layers with no steel.

questions.q: A seller replaced R-13 attic insulation with R-49. Compared with the old insulation, the new insulation:
c: Lets more heat pass through
Has the same thermal effect
Resists heat flow better
Is less fire resistant
questions.x: A higher R-value means greater resistance to heat flow, so R-49 insulates better. Assuming a higher number means more heat transfer confuses R-value with U-value.

questions.q: Gutters on a house are pulling away because the vertical board they are nailed to, running along the ends of the rafters, has rotted. That board is the:
c: Soffit
Ridge
Flashing
Fascia
questions.x: The fascia is the vertical trim across the rafter ends where gutters attach. The soffit is the horizontal underside of the overhang, the usual mix-up.

questions.q: Water stains appear on a ceiling right below where a skylight meets the roof. The component most likely to have failed is the:
c: Sheathing
Soffit vent
Flashing
Fascia
questions.x: Flashing seals the joint where a skylight, chimney or wall meets the roof. Sheathing lies under the roofing everywhere; the leak at a joint points to flashing.

questions.q: An inspector of a 1905 house finds wall studs running in one piece from the foundation to the roof, with no fire blocking between floors. This is:
c: Balloon framing
Platform framing
Post-and-beam framing
Steel stud framing
questions.x: Balloon framing uses continuous studs through two or more stories, and the open cavities let fire spread fast. Platform framing stops the studs at each floor, which is why it is the modern standard.

questions.q: Under GBL 777-a, defects in workmanship and materials in a new home (other than systems and structure) are warranted for:
c: 6 months
1 year
2 years
6 years
questions.x: General workmanship and materials carry 1 year. Two years covers plumbing, electrical, heating, cooling and ventilation; 6 years covers the load-bearing structure.

questions.q: Five years after buying a newly built home, the owner finds a cracked load-bearing beam caused by a construction defect. Under GBL 777-a the owner:
c: Has no claim, since every period has run
Has a claim for 10 years after closing
Has a claim if it is a plumbing failure
Has a claim, since structure carries 6 years
questions.x: Material defects in load-bearing structure are covered for 6 years, so year five is inside the window. The 'every period has run' choice applies the 1- and 2-year limits to the wrong component.

questions.q: A Dutchess County lot needs a new septic system. A licensed excavator offers to draw the design himself to save money. Under New York rules:
c: That is fine if the town approves it
The design needs an engineer or architect
The owner may design it with a permit
The building inspector draws the design
questions.x: A residential septic design must come from a NY licensed professional engineer or registered architect and be approved by the health department. The excavator can install it but cannot design it.

questions.q: Water poured into a test hole on a rural lot takes hours to drain away. For septic planning this suggests:
c: The soil percolates well
The well needs to be deeper
Absorption may be poor
The radon level is high
questions.x: A slow perc test means the soil absorbs wastewater poorly, which may need a larger field or an engineered system. A fast-draining hole is the one that percolates well.

questions.q: A homeowner signs a $12,000 kitchen remodeling contract on Monday and has second thoughts on Tuesday. Under New York's home improvement law, she:
c: Can cancel within 3 business days
Cannot cancel after signing
Can cancel within 30 days
Can cancel if work has not started
questions.x: Home improvement contracts must give notice of the owner's right to cancel within 3 business days. The 'not started' choice sounds fair but is not the statutory test.

questions.q: A buyer of a ranch house wants to run new plumbing under the floor. The agent warns this will be costly because the floor is a concrete slab poured on the ground with no crawl space. The house is:
c: Balloon framed
On a pier foundation
Slab-on-grade
A full basement
questions.x: With slab-on-grade, the slab is the floor and there is no space beneath it, so under-floor work means cutting concrete. A pier foundation leaves a crawl space, the opposite situation.

questions.q: A builder and owner disagree over which brand and grade of windows the contract called for. The document that should settle it is the:
c: Plat map
Certificate of occupancy
Survey
Specifications
questions.x: Specifications spell out materials, quality and methods in writing. A CO shows the building passed final inspection for its use, not which window grade was promised.

questions.q: Which sequence shows a typical load path from the top of a house to the soil?
c: Joists, rafters, footing, girder
Rafters, walls, girder, footing
Footing, girder, rafters, walls
Soffit, fascia, sill, footing
questions.x: Loads travel from rafters to walls, then through girders and columns to footings and the soil. The soffit and fascia choice uses real parts, but they are trim that carries no structural load.

questions.q: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one pound of water by one degree Fahrenheit is a:
c: Watt
Ton
BTU
Therm
questions.x: A British Thermal Unit is the standard heat measure for furnaces, boilers and AC. A therm is 100,000 BTU, and a ton of cooling is 12,000 BTU per hour.

questions.q: A buyer's central air conditioner is rated at 2.5 tons. Its cooling capacity is:
c: 25,000 BTU per hour
30,000 BTU per hour
12,500 BTU per hour
300,000 BTU per hour
questions.x: 1 ton = 12,000 BTU per hour, so 2.5 x 12,000 = 30,000. The 25,000 trap uses 10,000 BTU per ton.

questions.q: A heating system in which a furnace heats air and a blower distributes it through ducts is:
c: Forced warm air
Hot water baseboard
One-pipe steam
Radiant floor
questions.x: Forced warm air uses a furnace and ducts. Hot water and steam systems use a boiler with radiators or baseboards, and radiant floors use tubing or cables in the floor.

questions.q: In a prewar Manhattan co-op, an agent sees a boiler with a glass gauge showing the water level and cast iron radiators that hiss. The building most likely has:
c: Forced air heat
A heat pump
Steam heat
Hot water heat
questions.x: A sight glass on the boiler and hissing radiator vents are signs of steam. Hot water systems also use boilers and radiators, but they rely on a circulator pump and expansion tank and do not hiss.

questions.q: A system that heats in winter by extracting heat from outdoor air and cools in summer by reversing the cycle is a(n):
c: Boiler
Heat pump
Evaporative cooler
Furnace
questions.x: A heat pump moves heat in either direction. A boiler and furnace produce heat but cannot cool.

questions.q: In New York, a discovered petroleum spill from a home heating oil tank must be reported to the Department of Environmental Conservation within:
c: 24 hours
10 days
30 days
2 hours
questions.x: DEC requires petroleum spills to be reported within 2 hours of discovery. 24 hours is the common distractor because many other notice rules use a day.

questions.concept: Signs of a buried oil tank
questions.q: A house heated by natural gas has a capped pipe sticking out of the front lawn near the foundation. An agent should recognize this as a possible sign of:
c: An abandoned oil tank
A radon vent system
A septic tank cleanout
A lawn sprinkler riser
questions.x: Fill and vent pipes serve oil tanks. On a house now heated by gas, an outside pipe suggests an old UST that may still be buried; a radon system vents up the side of the house to the roofline, not from the lawn.

questions.q: Older galvanized steel water supply pipes commonly cause:
c: Rising supply water pressure
Rust and reduced flow
Sewer gas odors
Lead in the water
questions.x: Galvanized pipe corrodes inside and narrows over time, lowering pressure and flow. Lead in water is linked to lead service lines and lead solder, not galvanized steel itself.

questions.q: The purpose of a plumbing vent stack through the roof is to:
c: Let heat escape from the water heater
Keep traps sealed and vent sewer gas
Raise pressure in the supply lines
Ventilate the attic in hot weather
questions.x: Vents admit air to drain lines so trap seals are not siphoned dry, and carry sewer gas out above the roof. The water heater has its own flue, which is why the first choice tempts.

questions.q: Which device protects a circuit by tripping and can be reset rather than replaced?
c: Cartridge fuse
Circuit breaker
Step-down transformer
GFCI outlet
questions.x: A breaker trips and resets. A fuse has a metal strip that melts and must be replaced; a GFCI outlet also resets, but it guards against ground faults rather than circuit overload.

questions.q: Electrical wiring enclosed in a flexible spiral metal jacket is known as:
c: Romex
Knob and tube
BX cable
PVC conduit
questions.x: BX is armored cable with the wires inside a spiral metal jacket. Romex is nonmetallic sheathed cable in plastic, the most common mix-up.

questions.q: An inspector finds a 30-amp fuse protecting a circuit wired for 15 amps. The main danger is that:
c: The fuse will blow constantly
Voltage will drop to 60 volts
The house will lose its ground
The wire can overheat first
questions.x: An oversized fuse lets more current flow than the wire can safely carry, so the wire can overheat before the fuse blows. Constant blowing happens with an undersized fuse, the reverse case.

questions.q: Aluminum branch circuit wiring installed in some homes in the 1960s and 1970s is a concern because it:
c: Can loosen and overheat at connections
Cannot carry a 120-volt load
Contains lead in its insulation
Is banned from resale under New York law
questions.x: Aluminum expands, contracts and oxidizes at terminals, loosening connections that can overheat. Homes with it can be sold; repairs use approved connectors.

questions.q: Each of the following would typically be on a 240-volt circuit EXCEPT:
c: Electric range
Central AC condenser
Bedroom lighting
Electric clothes dryer
questions.x: Lighting and standard outlets run on 120 volts. Ranges, dryers, central AC and well pumps use 240 volts.

questions.q: Furnace and boiler output, such as "80,000 per hour," is stated in:
c: Amperes
BTUs
Volts
R-values
questions.x: Heating output is measured in British Thermal Units per hour. R-values rate insulation's resistance to heat flow, not heat output.

questions.q: A condenser is labeled 42,000 BTU per hour. What is its size in tons?
c: 3 tons
3.5 tons
4.2 tons
4 tons
questions.x: Divide by 12,000 BTU per ton: 42,000 / 12,000 = 3.5 tons. The 4.2 trap divides by 10,000.

questions.q: A house has registers in the floors, a return grille in the hallway, and a furnace with a blower and filter in the basement. It is heated by:
c: Forced warm air
Hot water
Steam
Electric baseboard
questions.x: Registers, returns, ducts and a blower mark a forced warm air system. Hot water systems also start in the basement, but they use a boiler and pipes, with no ducts or registers.

questions.q: Which feature is the clearest sign that a boiler system produces steam rather than hot water?
c: A circulator pump
An expansion tank
A sight glass
Baseboard fins
questions.x: A sight glass shows the water level in a steam boiler. A circulator pump and expansion tank are hallmarks of hot water systems, the opposite answer.

questions.q: A listing says one outdoor unit both heats and cools the home and there is no furnace or boiler. The system is most likely a:
c: Steam system
Heat pump
Forced air furnace
Swamp cooler
questions.x: A heat pump reverses its refrigerant cycle to heat or cool. A swamp (evaporative) cooler cools by evaporation but cannot heat.

questions.q: At 9:00 a.m., a plumber discovers heating oil leaking from a basement tank in a Long Island home. Under DEC rules, the spill should be reported by:
c: 11:00 a.m. that day
9:00 a.m. the next day
The end of the week
The next business day
questions.x: Petroleum spills must be reported to DEC within 2 hours of discovery. A 24-hour deadline feels reasonable, which makes 'next day' the trap.

questions.concept: Signs of a buried oil tank
questions.q: Which clue most strongly suggests an abandoned underground oil tank at a gas-heated house?
c: A vent pipe beside the foundation
A fan on a pipe up the side wall
A green patch over the leach field
A cleanout cap near the street
questions.x: Fill and vent pipes outside a house that no longer burns oil point to a tank left in the ground. A fan on a pipe running up the wall is a radon mitigation system, the tempting look-alike.

questions.q: In a 1950 house, water barely trickles from the upstairs taps and comes out rust-colored at first. The likely cause is:
c: Copper pipes
A failed vent stack
Corroded galvanized pipe
PEX supply lines
questions.x: Galvanized steel corrodes inside, narrowing the pipe and discoloring the water. A failed vent causes slow drains and odors, not weak, rusty supply water.

questions.q: Sewer gas smells in a bathroom and the sink drain gurgles when the tub empties. The most likely cause is:
c: A blocked plumbing vent
Low water pressure
An undersized water heater
Corroded supply pipes
questions.x: A blocked vent lets drains siphon trap seals dry, so gas escapes and drains gurgle. Corroded supply pipes affect incoming water, not the drain side.

questions.q: When a circuit protected by a fuse is overloaded, the fuse:
c: Trips and can be reset
Grounds the circuit
Lowers the voltage
Melts and is replaced
questions.x: A fuse contains a metal strip that melts, so the fuse must be replaced. Tripping and resetting describes a circuit breaker.

questions.q: Romex wiring is best described as:
c: Cable in a metal spiral jacket
Nonmetallic sheathed cable
Wires on porcelain knobs
Empty flexible metal conduit
questions.x: Romex is nonmetallic sheathed cable in a plastic jacket. The metal spiral jacket describes BX (armored cable), the usual mix-up.

questions.q: A circuit wired with 14-gauge wire rated for 15 amps should be protected by a fuse or breaker of:
c: 30 amps
20 amps
15 amps
60 amps
questions.x: The protective device should match the wire's rating, here 15 amps. A larger fuse lets the wire overheat before it blows, which is the fire risk.

questions.q: A home inspector reports aluminum branch wiring in a 1971 house. The practical advice to the buyer is that:
c: The house can't legally be sold
The wire can't carry 120 volts
An electrician should check it
The wiring contains asbestos
questions.x: The risk with aluminum wire is loose, overheating connections, which an electrician can fix with approved connectors. Nothing bars selling the house.

questions.q: Which household item normally runs on a 120-volt circuit?
c: Electric dryer
Well pump
Electric range
Table lamp
questions.x: Lighting and ordinary outlets use 120 volts. Dryers, ranges, central AC and well pumps draw 240 volts.

questions.q: Asbestos poses the greatest health risk when it is:
c: Encapsulated
Painted over
Enclosed in drywall
Friable
questions.x: Friable asbestos crumbles and releases fibers into the air. Encapsulated asbestos is sealed with a coating, which is a recognized way to make it safer, not more dangerous.

questions.q: Exposure to asbestos fibers is linked to each of the following EXCEPT:
c: Asbestosis
Pleural mesothelioma
Lung cancer
Lead poisoning
questions.x: Asbestos causes asbestosis, lung cancer and mesothelioma. Lead poisoning comes from lead paint, pipes and soil, a different hazard.

questions.q: Cutting a piece of suspect pipe insulation and sending it to a laboratory for analysis is:
c: Bulk sampling
Air monitoring
Wipe sampling
Encapsulation
questions.x: Bulk sampling analyzes the material itself. Air monitoring counts airborne fibers, and wipe sampling tests settled dust, so neither tests the insulation directly.

questions.q: The federal lead-based paint disclosure rule applies to the sale or lease of housing built:
c: After 1978
Before 1978
Before 1960
From 1960 to 1978
questions.x: The rule covers pre-1978 housing. The syllabus says "after 1978" in one place, a known typo that makes the first choice tempting.

questions.q: A buyer is purchasing a 1940 house. Under federal law, unless the buyer waives it in writing, the buyer must be given:
c: A lead abatement done by the seller
A lead inspection paid for by the seller
A 10-day opportunity to test for lead
A 3-day right to rescind after closing
questions.x: Buyers of pre-1978 housing get a 10-day opportunity to inspect. Sellers need not test or abate; they disclose known hazards and give the EPA pamphlet.

questions.q: The EPA recommends mitigation when indoor radon levels reach or exceed:
c: 4 picocuries per liter
1 picocurie per liter
10 picocuries per liter
2 picocuries per liter
questions.x: The EPA action level is 4 pCi/L. Between 2 and 4 EPA suggests considering mitigation, which makes 2 the tempting wrong number.

questions.q: The most common method of reducing radon in a house with a basement slab is:
c: Sealing basement wall cracks
Sub-slab depressurization
Running a dehumidifier
Adding attic ventilation
questions.x: A pipe and fan draw soil gas from under the slab and vent it above the roof. Sealing cracks helps, which is why it tempts, but it is not enough by itself.

questions.q: A homeowner in Rochester has 60 square feet of mold in a finished basement. Under New York's mold program, which is correct?
c: One contractor may assess and remediate under a single contract
No license is needed for mold in a private home
The county health department removes the mold
A licensed assessor and a separate licensed remediator
questions.x: NY Labor Law Article 32 requires DOL-licensed assessors and remediators for projects over 10 square feet, and they may not be the same firm on the same project. The single-contractor choice is exactly what the independence rule forbids.

questions.q: Insulation pumped into wall cavities in the 1970s that can release formaldehyde gas is:
c: UFFI
Fiberglass
Cellulose
Vermiculite
questions.x: Urea formaldehyde foam insulation off-gasses formaldehyde, especially when new. Vermiculite is the trap: it is linked to asbestos contamination, not formaldehyde.

questions.q: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), such as the refrigerant Freon, are an environmental concern because they:
c: Cause asbestosis
Deplete the ozone layer
Carry bacteria into wells
Release radon gas indoors
questions.x: CFCs destroy stratospheric ozone and were phased out under the Montreal Protocol and the Clean Air Act. Radon is a natural soil gas from uranium decay, unrelated to refrigerants.

questions.q: In New York, the professionals who apply pesticides to treat termite infestations must be certified by the:
c: Department of Agriculture and Markets
Department of Health
Department of Environmental Conservation
Department of Labor's license and certificate unit
questions.x: DEC certifies pesticide applicators, including those treating wood-destroying insects. The Department of Labor licenses asbestos and mold contractors, which makes it the tempting wrong pick.

questions.q: A buyer is worried about high-voltage transmission lines behind a house. Which statement about electromagnetic fields is most accurate?
c: They are proven to cause cancer for anyone living near a line
They fall under the federal lead disclosure rule
Health evidence is unsettled; fields fade with distance
They are a hazard the seller is required to remediate
questions.x: Research has not established a clear health link, and EMFs weaken quickly with distance. Buyers may still consider proximity material, but there is no remediation duty.

questions.q: Occupants of a tightly sealed office building report headaches and eye irritation that go away when they leave. This is commonly called:
c: Sick building syndrome
Building-related illness
Radon exposure
Legionnaires' disease
questions.x: Sick building syndrome describes symptoms tied to time in a building that ease after leaving. Building-related illness is the close distractor: it is a diagnosable illness with an identified cause, such as Legionnaires' disease, that does not clear up on leaving.

questions.q: Pipe wrap in a basement contains asbestos. It is intact and sealed, but the buyer plans to tear it out with a crowbar. The main concern is that removal will:
c: Make the material friable
Release radon from the soil
Expose lead in the pipes
Void the home warranty
questions.x: Disturbing intact asbestos crumbles it and releases fibers, which is why it is best left alone or removed by licensed contractors. Radon comes from soil gas, not from pipe wrap.

questions.q: Mesothelioma, a cancer of the lining of the chest or abdomen, is most closely linked to exposure to:
c: Radon gas
Formaldehyde
Lead dust
Asbestos
questions.x: Mesothelioma is the signature asbestos disease. Radon is linked to lung cancer, which makes it the tempting choice, but not to mesothelioma.

questions.q: After asbestos removal, a contractor checks whether fibers remain suspended in the room. This test is:
c: Bulk sampling
Air monitoring
A perc test
Encapsulation
questions.x: Air monitoring counts airborne fibers and is used to clear a work area after removal. Bulk sampling tests a piece of the material itself, before the work.

questions.q: Which sale requires the federal lead-based paint disclosure?
c: A house built in 1975
A house built in 1985
A lot with no building
A condo built in 1992
questions.x: The rule covers housing built before 1978, so the 1975 house is covered. The 1985 and 1992 choices exploit the syllabus typo that says 'after 1978.'

questions.q: When selling pre-1978 housing, a seller must do each of the following EXCEPT:
c: Give the EPA lead pamphlet
Disclose known lead hazards
Remove any lead paint found
Offer a 10-day testing window
questions.x: Federal law requires disclosure, the pamphlet and the buyer's 10-day opportunity to test, but it does not require the seller to abate. The testing window is real and can be waived in writing by the buyer.

questions.q: A basement radon test reads 5.2 pCi/L. Under EPA guidance, the buyer should:
c: Do nothing, it is below the limit
Plan to mitigate the radon
Retest if it tops 10 pCi/L
Call DEC within 2 hours
questions.x: Readings at or above the EPA action level of 4 pCi/L call for mitigation. The 2-hour DEC rule is for petroleum spills, not radon.

questions.q: A buyer sees a white PVC pipe running from the basement floor up the outside wall to above the roof, with a fan in the line. This is most likely a:
c: Plumbing vent stack
Radon mitigation system
Oil tank vent
Dryer exhaust
questions.x: Sub-slab depressurization draws soil gas through a pipe with a fan and vents it above the roof. A plumbing vent also exits the roof, but it has no fan and starts at the drain lines.

questions.q: In New York, licensed mold assessors and remediators are required for projects larger than:
c: 5 square feet
100 square feet
50 square feet
10 square feet
questions.x: Labor Law Article 32 applies to mold projects over 10 square feet, and the assessor and remediator must be independent of each other. 100 square feet is a figure from some older guidance, not the NY licensing trigger.

questions.q: An inspector finds crumbly, light-colored foam insulation that was injected into wall cavities in 1978. The chemical concern is:
c: Asbestos fibers
Formaldehyde gas
Radon gas
Lead dust
questions.x: This describes UFFI, which can release formaldehyde. Asbestos is linked to older pipe wrap, tiles and vermiculite, not foam injected into walls.

questions.q: Older air conditioners and refrigerators that use Freon raise an environmental concern because the refrigerant:
c: Contains asbestos
Releases radon
Harms the ozone layer
Contains lead
questions.x: Freon is a CFC that depletes stratospheric ozone, so it must be recovered properly. Asbestos turns up in old pipe and boiler insulation, not in refrigerant.

questions.q: A buyer wants proof that the exterminator treating a house for termites is properly certified in New York. The certification comes from the:
c: Department of State
Department of Labor
Department of Health
DEC
questions.x: DEC certifies commercial pesticide applicators. The Department of Labor licenses asbestos and mold contractors, the usual mix-up.

questions.q: A buyer asks whether the power lines along the rear lot line will make her family sick. The agent's best answer is that:
c: They are proven to cause cancer
They pose no risk whatsoever
Science is unsettled; she can look into it
The seller has to bury them first
questions.x: Evidence on EMF health effects is inconclusive, so the agent should not reassure or alarm, and should let the buyer research or consult experts. Saying 'no risk' overstates what the research shows.

questions.q: The most common cause of sick building syndrome in energy-efficient buildings is:
c: Buried oil tanks
Poor ventilation
Aluminum wiring
Radon in the soil
questions.x: Tightly sealed buildings with poor ventilation trap indoor pollutants. Radon is a soil gas problem in basements, not the usual cause of office-wide symptoms that ease after leaving.

questions.q: An environmental site assessment that reviews historical records, inspects the site, and interviews people, without taking samples, is a:
c: Phase III
Phase II
Phase IV
Phase I
questions.x: Phase I is investigative only. Phase II is the tempting pick because it is the next step, but it takes soil and groundwater samples.

questions.q: The phase of an environmental assessment that involves the actual cleanup of contamination is:
c: Phase I
Phase III
Phase II
Phase IV
questions.x: Phase III is remediation. Phase IV is the ongoing management and monitoring that follows cleanup.

questions.q: Liability under CERCLA (Superfund) is best described as:
c: Limited to the party that caused the pollution
Based on proof of negligence by the owner
Strict, joint and several, and retroactive
Capped at the property's purchase price
questions.x: CERCLA imposes liability without fault on current and past owners and others, and any one party can be required to pay the whole cost. The 'party that caused it' choice is how most people think liability should work, which is why it tempts.

questions.q: Before buying an industrial lot, an investor commissions a Phase I assessment that finds nothing. Years later, buried drums are discovered. The investor's best defense to Superfund liability is the:
c: Statute of limitations defense
Doctrine of laches
Doctrine of caveat emptor
Innocent landowner defense
questions.x: SARA (1986) created the innocent landowner defense for buyers who made all appropriate inquiry before purchase, and a clean Phase I supports it. Caveat emptor does not shield an owner from Superfund's strict liability.

questions.q: The federal law that sets standards for public drinking water systems is the:
c: Clean Air Act
Safe Drinking Water Act
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
Clean Water Act
questions.x: The SDWA regulates public water systems; it does not cover private household wells. The Clean Water Act regulates discharges into surface waters, not tap water.

questions.q: A buyer is purchasing a house with a private well in Westchester County. Which is true?
c: County law requires a well water test tied to the sale
Federal drinking water law covers the well, so no test is needed
The septic system is tested, but the well is not
The town assessor certifies the well water quality
questions.x: Westchester County requires private well testing on sale. The SDWA covers public systems, not private wells, so the federal-law choice is a misreading.

questions.q: Typical warning signs of a failing septic system include each of the following EXCEPT:
c: Soggy ground over the field
Sewage odors in the yard
Slow drains and backups
Low radon readings indoors
questions.x: Radon readings have nothing to do with septic function. Wet or unusually green fields, odors, and slow drains are classic signs of failure.

questions.concept: Agent duty to disclose known defects
questions.q: A seller tells his listing agent about a capped, buried oil tank and instructs the agent not to mention it. The agent should:
c: Follow it, since obedience is a fiduciary duty
Refuse to conceal it and disclose it
Complete the PCDS and mark the tank "unknown"
Have the tank removed without telling the seller
questions.x: Obedience covers lawful instructions only. Concealing a known material defect is misrepresentation, and the seller, not the agent, completes the PCDS truthfully.

questions.q: Which agency regulates freshwater and tidal wetlands in New York State?
c: Department of State
Department of Health
Department of Environmental Conservation
U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District
questions.x: DEC administers the state's freshwater and tidal wetlands laws. The Army Corps of Engineers regulates federal waters under the Clean Water Act, which makes it the tempting choice, but it is not the state regulator.

questions.q: When a buyer asks an agent whether a house has radon, the best response is to:
c: Say radon is unlikely in that area
Promise the seller will fix any problem
Repeat the seller's word that it is clean
Recommend a test by a qualified tester
questions.x: Agents should not act as experts or guarantee conditions. A test is the way to know a specific house's level; repeating the seller's assurance passes along an untested claim.

questions.q: A Phase I report on a former dry cleaner flags a possible solvent release. The lender asks for soil and groundwater samples. The next step is a:
c: Phase IV
Phase II
Phase III
Second Phase I
questions.x: Phase II samples soil and groundwater to confirm contamination. Phase III is the cleanup itself, which comes only after contamination is confirmed.

questions.q: Ongoing management and monitoring of a site after contamination has been cleaned up is part of:
c: Phase I
Phase II
Phase III
Phase IV
questions.x: Phase IV covers long-term management and monitoring after cleanup. Phase III is the remediation itself, the step just before.

questions.q: Three past owners of a Superfund site cannot be found or are bankrupt. The current owner, who did not pollute and did no due diligence, is sued for the full cleanup cost. Under CERCLA, the current owner:
c: Can be liable for the entire cost
Owes nothing, as it did not pollute
Owes a one-fourth share at most
Owes up to its purchase price
questions.x: Joint and several liability means any responsible party, including a current owner, can be made to pay all of it. 'One-fourth share' wrongly assumes liability is split evenly among owners.

questions.q: To qualify for the innocent landowner defense under SARA, a buyer generally must show it:
c: Paid fair market value
Made appropriate inquiry first
Owned the land under 5 years
Did not record the deed
questions.x: The defense requires all appropriate inquiry, usually a Phase I, before purchase. Paying fair value is irrelevant; it is the investigation that counts.

questions.q: A buyer assumes the Safe Drinking Water Act guarantees the quality of a country house's private well. The agent should explain that:
c: The Act covers public systems
The Act requires yearly well tests
The Act bans private wells
The town tests the well each spring
questions.x: The SDWA regulates public systems; testing a private well is the owner's job. The 'yearly well tests' choice invents a federal duty that does not exist.

questions.q: Outside of local rules such as Westchester County's, responsibility for testing a private household well generally rests with the:
c: Owner or buyer
EPA
Town assessor
Water utility
questions.x: No federal law tests private wells, so the owner or buyer arranges it. The EPA sets public system standards under the SDWA, which do not reach private wells.

questions.q: In midsummer, the grass over one patch of a rural backyard is unusually lush and green, and the ground there stays soggy. A buyer should suspect:
c: A failing septic field
A buried oil tank
High radon levels
A gas line leak
questions.x: Effluent surfacing over the absorption field feeds lush grass and keeps the soil wet, a classic septic failure sign. A gas leak tends to kill grass, not green it up.

questions.concept: Agent duty to disclose known defects
questions.q: A listing agent knows the basement floods every spring. The seller says nothing in writing. If a buyer asks, the agent:
c: Must disclose it
Can stay silent
Should say "unknown"
Needs a lawyer's okay
questions.x: Agents may not conceal known material defects, whatever the seller wants. Answering 'unknown' when the agent knows otherwise is misrepresentation.

questions.q: An owner wants to fill a marshy corner of a Long Island lot that is mapped as a state tidal wetland. The state permit comes from the:
c: Department of Health
Department of State
Town assessor
DEC
questions.x: DEC administers the state's tidal and freshwater wetlands permits. The Department of State runs coastal management programs, which tempts, but it does not issue wetlands permits.

questions.q: A buyer asks whether a house has a mold problem. The seller assured the agent it does not. The agent's best response is to:
c: Tell the buyer there is no mold
Promise the seller will clean it
Suggest a qualified inspection
Say mold is common and harmless
questions.x: Agents should not vouch for conditions they cannot verify; they should point the buyer to a qualified professional. Passing along the seller's assurance as fact is the trap.

questions.q: A buyer's agent finds no certificate of occupancy on file for a Brooklyn two-family built in 1931 and never altered. The most accurate conclusion is:
c: The house cannot be sold until the owner obtains a new CO
The house may be legal without one, since it predates 1938
The house is presumed to be an illegal conversion
The house needs a CO if the buyer finances the purchase with a loan
questions.x: NYC did not require COs for buildings completed before 1938, so an unaltered 1931 two-family can be legal without one; a Letter of No Objection can confirm the use. The tempting answer treats the missing CO as a bar to sale. It is not, although a later change in use, egress or occupancy would require a new CO.

questions.q: A Queens house built in 1925 had no CO. In 2024 the owner converted the cellar into a separate third apartment. Which statement is most accurate?
c: The pre-1938 exemption still applies, so no CO is needed
A Letter of No Objection is enough to legalize the new unit
The change in occupancy ends the exemption; a CO is required
No CO is needed as long as the cellar unit is not rented out
questions.x: The pre-1938 exemption lasts only while the building's use, egress and occupancy stay as built. Adding a dwelling unit changes occupancy, which requires a new CO. A Letter of No Objection is the tempting answer, but it confirms an existing legal use; it does not approve a new apartment.

questions.q: An inspector opens a ceiling above an interior wall and sees the floor joists overlapping and nailed together directly over it. This most strongly suggests the wall is:
c: A bearing wall
A curtain wall
A partition wall
A party wall
questions.x: Joists spliced over a wall are using it as support, so it is bearing and cannot come out without a beam to replace it. Partition is the tempting answer because the wall is interior, but a partition carries only itself. A party wall is shared between two attached buildings, not an interior wall.

questions.q: Each of the following suggests an interior wall may be bearing EXCEPT:
c: Floor joists above it overlap and are spliced over the wall
A girder or second wall sits directly below it in the basement
It runs perpendicular to the joists near the middle of their span
It runs parallel to the joists and sits between two of them
questions.x: A wall parallel to the joists, sitting between them, usually carries no floor load; it is typically a partition. Lapped joists, a support stacked below, and a perpendicular wall at midspan are all classic signs of a bearing wall. The tempting wrong pick is the perpendicular wall, but that orientation is exactly how bearing walls catch joists.

questions.concept: Lintel vs header vs flitch plate
questions.q: A steel angle set over a new window opening in a brick wall to carry the masonry above it is a:
c: Lintel
Header
Flitch plate
Sill plate
questions.x: A lintel spans an opening in masonry and carries the brick or stone above. A header does the same job in a wood stud wall, which is why it is the tempting answer. A flitch plate is steel sandwiched between wood beam members, and a sill plate is the wood member bolted to the top of the foundation.

questions.concept: Lintel vs header vs flitch plate
questions.q: To open a kitchen without lowering the ceiling, a contractor bolts a steel plate between two 2x10s to form a stronger beam of the same depth. The beam is a:
c: Steel lintel
Flitch plate beam
Built-up girder beam
Header joist
questions.x: A flitch plate beam sandwiches steel between wood to add strength without adding depth. A lintel is the tempting answer because it is often steel, but a lintel spans an opening in masonry. A ridge beam sits at the roof peak, and a header joist frames around an opening in a floor.

questions.q: A new steel column under a beam end stands directly on a thin basement floor slab, and the slab has cracked around it. What is the proper correction?
c: Pour a footing sized for the load under a new lally column
Add a second column right next to the first to share the load
Fill the cracks with epoxy and recheck them in one year
Replace the column with a wood post that spreads the load
questions.x: A lally column must sit on its own footing, a concrete pad sized for the load and wider than what it supports. The tempting answer is a second column, but it still pushes on the same thin slab. Epoxy only hides the crack. A wood post does not spread the load enough to fix a missing footing.

questions.q: In a typical house load path, a lally column transfers the load of a girder directly to:
c: The sill plate
A floor joist
Its own footing
The roof rafters
questions.x: Load travels down: joists to the girder, girder to the lally column, column to its own footing, and footing into the soil. The sill plate is the tempting answer because it is also low in the house, but it sits on the foundation wall and carries the wood frame, not a column load.

questions.q: An attic has R-19 batts on the floor. The owner adds a layer of blown cellulose rated R-30 on top. The total R-value is about:
questions.x: R-values of layers stacked in series add: 19 plus 30 equals R-49, and a higher number means better resistance to heat flow. R-24.5 is the trap: it averages the layers. R-30 counts only the bigger layer, and R-11 subtracts them.

questions.q: Which wall assembly offers the most resistance to heat flow?
c: R-15 batts alone
R-13 batts plus R-5 rigid foam
R-11 batts plus R-3 foam board
R-19 batts compressed to half thickness
questions.x: Layers add, so R-13 plus R-5 gives R-18, the highest here. R-11 plus R-3 is only R-14. Compressed batts are the trap: squeezing insulation removes the trapped air that gives it resistance, so a crushed R-19 performs well below its label.

questions.q: The written portion of a construction package that states materials, grades, brands and installation methods is the:
c: Blueprint
Specifications
Building permit
Survey
questions.x: Specifications describe the work in words: what materials, what grade, what method. Blueprints are the tempting answer because they come in the same package, but they are the drawings. A permit is the government's approval, and a survey locates the lot lines and improvements.

questions.q: A buyer wants to confirm a listing's claim of "R-21 walls and spray-foamed rim joists." Which document from the builder will state this most directly?
c: The floor plan
The certificate of occupancy
The specifications
The site survey
questions.x: Insulation types and R-values are written out in the specifications. A floor plan shows room layout and dimensions, not materials. The CO is the tempting answer because it is issued after inspections, but it certifies legal use and occupancy; it does not list materials.

questions.q: Under New York's housing merchant implied warranty, defects in the installation of a new home's heating system are covered for:
c: 1 year
2 years
6 years
10 years
questions.x: Plumbing, electrical, heating, cooling and ventilation installation defects are covered for 2 years from the warranty date. One year covers general workmanship and materials, which is the tempting answer for a furnace that simply stops working. Six years covers material defects in load-bearing parts.

questions.q: Three years after buying a new home from the builder, an owner finds the main girder cracked and the floor above sagging. Under the implied warranty, the claim is:
c: Too late, because the 2-year period ended
Covered, as a material defect within 6 years
Too late, because the 1-year period ended
Covered, because every defect is covered for 10 years
questions.x: A failure of a load-bearing part that affects its function is a material defect, covered for 6 years. The 2-year period is the tempting answer because it is the longest one most people remember, but it applies to mechanical systems. Ten years is not a statutory period, though some limited warranties offer it.

questions.q: A builder's contract for a new single-family home says the home is sold "as is" with no warranties, and no other warranty is offered. The clause is:
c: Valid if the buyer signs it
Valid if printed in bold type
Void as to the implied warranty
Valid if the buyer has an inspection
questions.x: A contract term excluding or modifying the housing merchant implied warranty is void unless the builder offers a limited warranty meeting the statute's minimum terms. A signature is the tempting answer, but the statute treats the warranty as public policy that cannot be signed away by a bare clause. Bold type and inspections do not change that.

questions.q: A builder's limited warranty may replace the implied warranty. It may do all of the following EXCEPT:
c: Exclude owners who buy from the first purchaser
Require written notice of claims by certified mail
Cover structural defects for 10 years
Cover heating and cooling installation for 1 year
questions.x: A limited warranty must at least match the statutory periods, so 1 year on systems falls short of the required 2. It may exclude later owners, set a written claims procedure, and give longer coverage than the law requires. Excluding later owners is the tempting answer, but the statute expressly permits it.

questions.q: Buyers of a new home move in on April 10 under an occupancy agreement and close on May 1. The certificate of occupancy issued April 5. The warranty periods begin on:
c: April 5
April 10
May 1
June 1
questions.x: The warranty date is the earlier of title passing to the first owner-occupant or that owner's first occupancy as a residence. Move-in on April 10 comes first. May 1 is the tempting answer because closing is usually the start, but only when the buyers move in after closing. The CO date does not start the warranty.

questions.q: A new home's warranty date was March 1, Year 1. The owner discovers a plumbing installation defect in February, Year 3. Written notice must reach the builder no later than about:
c: March 31, Year 2
March 1, Year 2
March 31, Year 3
March 1, Year 7
questions.x: The 2-year systems period ends March 1, Year 3, and written notice must be received no later than 30 days after the period expires, so about March 31, Year 3. March 31, Year 2 is the trap: it applies the 1-year workmanship period to a plumbing installation defect.

questions.q: Under New York's home improvement law, a contract for $12,000 of kitchen work in an owner's home must:
c: Be written, with notice of a 3-business-day right to cancel
Be in writing if the contractor asks the owner for a deposit
Be filed with the county clerk before work starts
Be reviewed by the owner's attorney to be enforceable
questions.x: Home improvement contracts over $500 must be written and include the dates, a description of the work and materials, and notice of the owner's 3-business-day cancellation right. The deposit is the tempting hook, but the writing requirement applies to every such contract, deposit or not; deposits add the escrow or bond rule.

questions.q: A contractor takes a $15,000 deposit on a $30,000 roof job and deposits it in his business checking account to buy materials for other jobs. Under New York's home improvement law, the main problem is that:
c: Deposits may not exceed 25% of the contract price
Advance payments must be escrowed or bonded
The owner must pay suppliers directly, not the contractor
A contractor may not accept deposits on roofing work
questions.x: Payments received before the work is substantially completed must be held in escrow or protected by a bond or similar arrangement. A cap on deposits is the tempting answer because it sounds like consumer protection, but the statute's rule is about protecting the money, not capping the amount.

questions.concept: Mechanic's lien on a single-family home
questions.q: A supplier delivered materials for a renovation of a single-family home and was not paid. It generally must file a mechanic's lien within how long after its last delivery?
c: 4 months
8 months
1 year
30 days
questions.x: For a single-family dwelling the general deadline is 4 months after the last work or materials; for other property it is 8 months. The 8-month rule is the tempting answer because it is the one usually quoted first. One year is how long a filed lien lasts without a foreclosure action.

questions.concept: Mechanic's lien on a single-family home
questions.q: An electrician finished work on a 12-unit apartment building on March 1 and was not paid. Generally, the lien must be filed by about:
c: July 1
September 1
November 1
March 1 of the next year
questions.x: For property other than a single-family dwelling, the deadline is generally 8 months after the last work, so about November 1. July 1 is the trap: it applies the 4-month single-family rule to an apartment building.

questions.q: Before closing on a new house with a private well and septic system upstate, which item best confirms the septic system was installed as approved?
c: The builder's sworn statement of compliance
A dye test run by the buyers
The well's flow test result
The designer's as-built certification
questions.x: Septic systems are designed by a licensed engineer or registered architect and approved by the health department; the as-built drawing and certification show it was built that way. A dye test is the tempting answer, but it only checks for surfacing effluent at a moment in time. A flow test measures the well, not the septic.

questions.q: Lenders and buyers of an upstate home on a private well most commonly require a certified lab test for:
c: Radon in the soil
Water hardness
Lead in the paint
Bacteria
questions.x: A well test by a state-certified lab for coliform bacteria, plus a flow test, is the standard before closing. Hardness is the tempting answer because it is common in wells, but it is a nuisance, not a health test lenders require. Radon and lead paint are separate tests.

questions.q: An inspector finds a boiler with a circulator pump, an expansion tank on the supply pipe, and finned baseboard in each room. The system is:
c: Hot water heat
Steam heat
Forced warm air
Radiant electric heat
questions.x: Circulator, expansion tank and finned baseboard identify a hot water (hydronic) system. Steam is the tempting answer because it also uses a boiler, but steam systems show a sight glass and radiators and do not need a circulator. Forced air uses a furnace and ducts.

questions.q: All of the following point to a forced warm air system EXCEPT:
c: Supply and return registers
A blower and a filter
A boiler sight glass
Ducts running to each room
questions.x: A sight glass shows the water level in a steam boiler, so it points to steam heat. Registers, ducts, a blower and a filter are all parts of forced air. Registers are the tempting pick for people who confuse them with radiators, but registers are the grilles where ducted air enters a room.

questions.q: A central air system is rated at 42,000 BTU per hour. Its capacity in tons is:
c: 3.0 tons
4.2 tons
4.0 tons
3.5 tons
questions.x: One ton of cooling equals 12,000 BTU per hour, so 42,000 divided by 12,000 is 3.5 tons. The tempting 4.2 comes from dividing by 10,000.

questions.q: A house's heat loss on the coldest day is 48,000 BTU per hour. Its existing boiler delivers 120,000 BTU per hour. By how many times is the boiler oversized?
c: 2.5 times
1.5 times
2.0 times
3.0 times
questions.x: 120,000 divided by 48,000 is 2.5, so the boiler is two and a half times the peak need, which means short cycling and wasted fuel. The tempting 2.0 rounds the ratio down and ignores the arithmetic.

questions.q: Why does an air-source heat pump usually cost less to run than electric baseboard heat?
c: It uses 240 volts while baseboard uses 120 volts
It burns natural gas whenever it gets cold out
It moves heat instead of making it
It heats water, which holds heat better than air
questions.x: A heat pump uses electricity to move heat, delivering more heat than the electricity it consumes, while resistance baseboard converts electricity to heat one for one. The voltage answer is the trap: both commonly use 240-volt circuits, and voltage does not set efficiency.

questions.q: A Westchester owner choosing between new electric baseboard and a cold-climate heat pump asks which costs less to install and which costs less to run. The best answer is:
c: Heat pump is cheaper both to install and to run
Baseboard is cheaper to install; heat pump to run
Baseboard is cheaper both to install and to run
Heat pump is cheaper to install; baseboard to operate
questions.x: Electric baseboard is inexpensive to install but converts electricity to heat one for one, so it is costly to operate. A heat pump costs more up front and much less to run because it moves heat. The tempting answer gives the heat pump both wins, which ignores its higher equipment cost.

questions.q: A 30-amp breaker protects a circuit wired with 14-gauge copper, which is rated for 15 amps. The main danger is that the:
c: Breaker will trip whenever two appliances run
Wire can overheat before the breaker trips
Circuit will run at 240 volts instead of 120
Outlets will lose their ground connection
questions.x: A breaker is sized to protect the wire. With a breaker twice the wire's rating, current can overheat the wire in the wall before the breaker reacts, a fire risk. Frequent tripping is the tempting answer, but a larger breaker trips less, which is exactly the problem.

questions.q: An old fuse box has a 30-amp fuse screwed into a socket for a 15-amp lighting circuit. This is a problem because the:
c: Fuse is too small and will blow constantly
Fuse no longer protects the 15-amp wiring
Circuit now needs a GFCI outlet to operate
Lights will dim whenever the fuse heats up
questions.x: Like a mismatched breaker, an oversized fuse lets more current flow than the wire can safely carry, defeating the protection. The tempting answer treats a 30-amp fuse as too small; it is twice the right size, so it blows too late, not too often.

questions.q: In a typical residential service upgrade, which item is generally the utility's responsibility?
c: The main panel
The meter base, mast and weatherhead
The meter and service drop
The branch circuits
questions.x: The utility brings power to the property (overhead drop or underground lateral) and owns the meter. The owner is responsible from the service entrance in: mast, meter base, service cable, panel and circuits. The meter base is the tempting answer because the meter sits in it, but the base belongs to the owner.

questions.q: When a homeowner upgrades from 100-amp to 200-amp service, the owner's electrician typically handles all of the following EXCEPT:
c: Installing the new main panel
Replacing the meter base
Running the new service cable
Supplying the meter
questions.x: The meter belongs to the utility, which supplies and sets it. The owner's licensed electrician installs the panel, meter base and service entrance cable under a permit. The meter base is the tempting wrong pick, but it is owner equipment even though the utility's meter plugs into it.

questions.q: A sink drains with a gurgle and the room smells of sewer gas. The most likely cause is:
c: A trap with no vent, losing its seal
A water heater set too low
Galvanized supply pipe rusting inside
A meter valve partly closed at the curb
questions.x: Traps hold water to block sewer gas, and a vent keeps draining water from siphoning that seal. A missing vent produces gurgling and odor. Rusting galvanized pipe is the tempting answer, but that affects supply pressure, not drains or sewer gas.

questions.q: Water pressure is weak on the second floor of a 1950s house. The water service is the original half-inch galvanized steel. The likely cause and fix are:
c: A missing vent stack; add a vent
Too large a trap; shorten the trap
A dry trap; run water to refill it
Rust narrowing the pipe; replace it
questions.x: Galvanized steel rusts from the inside, narrowing the pipe and cutting flow, especially to upper floors; replacing the service with a properly sized line is the fix. A missing vent is the tempting answer, but vents serve the drain side, not supply pressure.

questions.q: A seller of a 1955 house had a lead inspection done eight years ago that found lead paint on the windows. Under the federal disclosure rule, the seller must:
c: Disclose it if the buyer asks for it in writing
Retest, since reports over five years old expire
Remove the lead paint before signing any contract
Disclose it and provide the report
questions.x: Sellers of pre-1978 housing must disclose known lead-based paint and hazards and provide all available records and reports, with no age limit on a report. Retesting is the tempting answer, but the rule requires disclosure, not new testing or removal.

questions.q: For the sale of a 1970 house, the federal lead rule requires all of the following EXCEPT:
c: Giving the buyer the EPA lead pamphlet
A lead warning statement in the contract
Removing any lead paint before closing
Providing any available lead reports
questions.x: The rule is about disclosure and an opportunity to test: pamphlet, warning statement, disclosure of known hazards, and available reports. It never requires the seller to remove lead paint. The pamphlet is the tempting pick for people who think it applies only to rentals, but it applies to sales too.

questions.q: A buyer of a 1940 home wants to skip the lead inspection opportunity to make an offer more competitive. The buyer may:
c: Waive it in writing in the contract or addendum
Waive it by a phone call to the listing agent
Not waive it, since the 10 days cannot be waived
Waive it, with a lender's written approval
questions.x: The 10-day opportunity may be waived or changed, but in writing. The tempting answer says it cannot be waived; it can, though agents should make sure the buyer understands the trade-off, especially with young children in the home.

questions.q: Under the federal rule, a buyer of pre-1978 housing has how long to have the home tested for lead, unless the parties agree otherwise?
c: 3 days
10 days
7 days
30 days
questions.x: The rule gives the buyer a 10-day opportunity to test, which may be lengthened, shortened or waived in writing. Three days is the tempting answer because it is the right-of-rescission period in other consumer laws, not the lead rule.

questions.q: A short-term radon test for a home sale reads 2.4 pCi/L, but the inspector learns the seller kept basement windows open during the test. The result is:
c: Valid, since anything under 4 is a pass
Valid, if the test ran at least 48 hours
Unreliable; retest with the house closed
Unreliable, because tests have to run 90 days
questions.x: Radon tests require closed-house conditions before and during the test; open windows dilute the reading. The tempting answer accepts 2.4 as under the 4 pCi/L action level, but a test run under the wrong conditions does not measure the house. Short-term tests for sales commonly run 2 to 4 days; 90 days is long-term testing.

questions.q: After a sub-slab radon system is installed, the buyer wants proof it works. The best evidence is:
c: The contractor's paid invoice
The seller's written statement
A fan running sound in the basement
A post-mitigation radon test
questions.x: Only a new test, run after the system has operated and under closed-house conditions, shows the level dropped. The invoice is the tempting answer because it proves installation, but not results. EPA's action level remains 4 pCi/L.

questions.q: Old 9 by 9 inch vinyl floor tiles, intact under carpet, may contain asbestos. The best initial advice to a buyer is:
c: Scrape them up before moving in
Sample them and leave them alone
Sand them flat and paint over them
Wet-mop them weekly to remove fibers
questions.x: Asbestos is hazardous when friable or disturbed so fibers become airborne. Intact tiles are low risk; testing tells you what you have, and any removal goes to licensed abatement contractors. Scraping them up is the tempting answer and the riskiest choice.

questions.q: A Queens homeowner plans a renovation requiring a DOB permit. Before the permit issues, the owner must generally show asbestos requirements are met by:
c: A licensed home inspector's letter
A DEC asbestos handling license issued to the owner
An asbestos investigator's survey or exemption
A licensed plumber's affidavit
