First meeting with Leo about his {hood} condo loan. Jordan pulls up a chair. Leo has questions, and one of them is about how you get paid.

say: Here's my credit card for the application fee. Let's get going, my contingency is 45 days.
Take my card now so we don't lose time. What's the fee?

moves.text: Before any fee, we sign the pre-application disclosure and the fee agreement. It says what's refundable.
moves.fb: Correct. NY mortgage brokers give the pre-application disclosure and fee agreement, signed by both, before accepting fees.
moves.react: Okay. Read me the refundable part.

moves.text: Disclosure first, card second. It says I'm not the lender, what I charge, and what's refundable.
moves.fb: Right. No fee until the pre-application disclosure and fee agreement are signed.

moves.text: I'll take the card now and email the disclosure tonight. It's the same information either way, Leo.
moves.fb: The order matters: the disclosure and fee agreement come before any fee.

moves.text: Great, I'll run it now and send the paperwork later. Time is tight with a 45-day contingency.
moves.fb: Taking a fee before the pre-application disclosure and fee agreement violates DFS rules.

moves.text: No fees ever. Lenders pay mortgage brokers everything, so borrowers never owe a broker a single dime.
moves.fb: Not true in general. Brokers may be paid by the borrower or the lender, and it must be disclosed.

moves.text: I'll charge it now and refund it if the loan doesn't close. That's the standard fee agreement anyway.
moves.fb: Refund terms belong in the signed agreement before any fee is taken.

say: Jordan: "Quick thought, Tasha. My firm wants to start doing mortgages. If we arranged Leo's loan ourselves, what would we need?"
Jordan: "Could Hudson and Hart broker loans for our own buyers? What's involved?"

moves.text: DFS registration, licensed originators, and a dual agency disclosure signed by buyer and seller.
moves.fb: Right. A real estate broker acting as mortgage broker in the same deal must give the Banking Law dual agency disclosure.

moves.text: Register with DFS, use NMLS-licensed originators, give the mortgage dual agency disclosure.
moves.fb: Correct. DOS licensing doesn't cover mortgage brokering; DFS and the SAFE Act do.

moves.text: Some paperwork with the state, I think. Ask DFS what they want, since rules keep changing.
moves.fb: Vague. Name the requirements: DFS registration, MLO licenses, dual agency disclosure.

moves.text: Nothing extra, your real estate license covers it. DOS licensees can arrange loans for their clients.
moves.fb: A DOS real estate license does not authorize mortgage brokering. DFS registration and MLO licensing are required.

moves.text: Just give the RPL 443 dual agency form. That covers both the sale and the loan in one shot, Jordan.
moves.fb: The Banking Law mortgage dual agency disclosure is separate from RPL 443.

moves.text: You'd need a DOS broker license upgrade. Associate brokers can arrange mortgages, salespeople can't.
moves.fb: Mortgage brokering is regulated by DFS, not DOS license levels.

say: How do you get paid? Is the lender paying you to push me into a higher rate?
Be straight. Do you make more if my rate is higher?

moves.text: I'm paid by you or the lender, never both, and my pay can't depend on your rate. It's all disclosed.
moves.fb: Accurate summary of loan originator compensation rules and disclosure.

moves.text: No. Federal rules bar pay tied to your rate. Any lender credit for a higher rate goes to you.
moves.fb: Correct. LO compensation can't vary with loan terms, and lender credits are disclosed.

moves.text: It's complicated, but it works out fairly for everyone. You'll see the numbers at closing.
moves.fb: Evasive. Borrowers are entitled to clear disclosure of broker compensation up front.

moves.text: Don't worry about it. Brokers are paid by the bank, so it doesn't cost you anything at all, Leo.
moves.fb: Borrowers are entitled to disclosure of broker compensation, including any lender rebate.

moves.text: Yes, a bit more on higher rates, but I'd never abuse it. Every broker in New York works that way, honestly.
moves.fb: Compensation that varies with the rate is prohibited for loan originators.

moves.text: I'm paid by both you and the lender. It's how I keep my fee low on each side of the deal for you.
moves.fb: A broker may be paid by the borrower or the lender on a loan, not both.

say: Rates jumped last week. Can I protect today's rate? The closing is in 50 days.
Can we lock today's rate? Closing's about 50 days out.

moves.text: I can lock 60 days in writing: rate, points, expiration date. If closing slips, extending may cost you.
moves.fb: Correct. Rate locks must be written and state terms and expiration; the lock should cover the expected closing.

moves.text: Let's lock past the closing, 60 days, all in writing: rate, points, and when it expires.
moves.fb: Right. A lock that covers the closing date, documented in writing.

moves.text: I'll lock for 30 days to save the fee. We can always extend it later if the closing runs long.
moves.fb: Legal but weak. A 30-day lock on a 50-day closing almost guarantees an extension fee or a new rate.

moves.text: Consider it locked. I'll remember today's rate, and the lender will honor it when we get to closing.
moves.fb: A lock must be in writing with its terms and expiration. A verbal promise protects no one.

moves.text: Locks only exist for loans over $1 million. For yours, we float until closing and hope for the best.
moves.fb: Locks are available on standard loans. Leave the decision with Leo, in writing.

moves.text: I'll lock for 120 days to be safe. Longer locks cost the same as short ones at every lender I use.
moves.fb: Longer locks usually cost more. Match the lock to the closing.

say: Jordan: "Day 40. The seller's attorney is asking whether Leo's preapproval letter satisfies the mortgage contingency."
Jordan: "Seller's side wants to know: does the preapproval count for the contingency?"

moves.text: No. The contingency needs the written commitment. I expect it by day 42 and will send it.
moves.fb: Correct. A preapproval is not a commitment. The commitment for the specific property satisfies the contingency.

moves.text: A preapproval doesn't satisfy it. I'll send the commitment to both attorneys the day it's issued.
moves.fb: Right. Only a written commitment satisfies a mortgage contingency.

moves.text: Tell them we're very close. The commitment should come soon, I just can't give them a date yet.
moves.fb: Honest, but vague. Give the status and expected timing so the attorneys can plan.

moves.text: Sure, tell them the preapproval counts. It's basically the same thing as a commitment anyway.
moves.fb: Misstating loan status to the other side is a misrepresentation. Only a commitment satisfies the contingency.

moves.text: Send them the prequalification letter too. Together with the preapproval, it's equal to a commitment.
moves.fb: Prequalification is weaker still. Only a written commitment for the property satisfies it.

moves.text: Tell them the loan is already approved. We'll catch up on the paperwork before anyone checks.
moves.fb: A false statement about loan status is a misrepresentation that can blow up the deal.

say: Jordan, after Leo steps out: "I send you a lot of buyers. Any chance of $500 a referral?"
Jordan: "Could you kick back a little for every client I send your way?"

moves.text: I can't. Referral fees on settlement services break RESPA, even if they're disclosed.
moves.fb: Correct. RESPA Section 8 bans referral fees, and disclosure doesn't cure it.

moves.text: No referral fees, ever. RESPA bars them, and it would put both of our licenses at risk.
moves.fb: Right. Kickbacks between settlement providers are prohibited.

moves.text: Maybe a gift card now and then, nothing formal. That's how most people in the business do it.
moves.fb: A thing of value for referrals is still a kickback under RESPA.

moves.text: Sure, as long as we put it in writing and disclose it to the buyers. Then it's perfectly legal.
moves.fb: Disclosure doesn't legalize a RESPA referral fee.

moves.text: Sure, I'll pay your broker instead of you. Payments to a firm aren't referral fees at all.
moves.fb: Routing it through the firm doesn't change anything.

moves.text: Only if it's under $100. Small referral payments are allowed under federal rules.
moves.fb: There's no small-amount exception.

say: The quote mentions points. What are they, and should I pay them?
Should I buy points to lower my rate?

moves.text: A point is 1% of the loan and lowers the rate. It pays off only if you keep the loan long enough.
moves.fb: Correct. Discount points are prepaid interest; the break-even depends on the time horizon.
moves.react: So if I stay ten years, maybe.

moves.text: Each point costs 1% of the loan and buys a lower rate. I'll show the break-even month.
moves.fb: Right. Explain the math and let Leo decide.

moves.text: Most people don't bother with points. I'd skip them and keep the cash for your moving costs.
moves.fb: Maybe reasonable, but you skipped the explanation he asked for.

moves.text: One point is 1% of the purchase price, so on this condo it's a pretty big chunk of money.
moves.fb: A point is 1% of the loan amount, not the price.

moves.text: Points raise your rate but lower your closing costs. That's exactly why the lenders pay them to you.
moves.fb: Backwards. Discount points are paid by the borrower to lower the rate; lender credits do the reverse.

moves.text: Always buy as many points as you can afford. It's guaranteed to save money over any loan term.
moves.fb: Not guaranteed. If he sells or refinances early, points may never pay off.

say: My loan's about $900,000. Is that a jumbo? Someone said jumbos are harder.
Is a $900,000 loan jumbo in New York City?

moves.text: Not here. In high-cost areas like NYC the conforming limit goes up to $1,249,125 in 2026.
moves.fb: Correct. The baseline is $832,750, but high-cost areas go up to $1,249,125.

moves.text: The baseline limit is $832,750, but NYC is high-cost, so $900,000 is still conforming.
moves.fb: Right. Location matters for the conforming limit.

moves.text: Probably jumbo, but it doesn't matter. Rates are similar these days on both kinds.
moves.fb: You missed the high-cost limit. Check the actual numbers.

moves.text: Yes, anything over $832,750 is a jumbo everywhere in the country, with no exceptions at all.
moves.fb: High-cost areas have a higher conforming limit.

moves.text: Jumbo starts at $1 million. Below that, every loan in America counts as conforming.
moves.fb: Wrong threshold. The baseline is $832,750, higher in high-cost areas.

moves.text: Jumbo loans are illegal for first-time buyers in New York, so we'll split it in two.
moves.fb: No such rule. And splitting loans to dodge limits isn't a plan.

say: My bonus is coming in March. Can you just put a bit more income on the application now?
Can you round my income up? I'll make it next year anyway.

moves.text: No. The application matches what you can document today. I'll show the lender your bonus history.
moves.fb: Correct. Overstating income is mortgage fraud. Documented bonus history can count.
moves.react: Okay, I have two years of bonuses.

moves.text: I won't inflate it. If your bonus is steady and documented, underwriting may count it.
moves.fb: Right. Honest application, documented income.

moves.text: Let's leave it as is for now and see if the loan works. If not, we can talk about it later on.
moves.fb: Not wrong today, but 'talk about it later' leaves the door open. Say no clearly.

moves.text: Sure, a small bump is fine. Underwriters only spot-check it, and you'll earn it anyway pretty soon.
moves.fb: Overstating income on a loan application is mortgage fraud, whatever the amount.

moves.text: I'll put it in as projected income. Lenders count future raises if you're confident about them.
moves.fb: Unverified future income can't be used to qualify.

moves.text: I'll add it as other income. Other income doesn't need any documents at all in underwriting.
moves.fb: All qualifying income must be documented.

roleplays.debrief: You practised mortgage broker rules in New York: sign the pre-application disclosure and fee agreement before taking any fee, and a real estate firm brokering its own buyers' loans needs DFS registration, licensed originators and the Banking Law dual agency disclosure. Originator pay can't vary with the rate and comes from the borrower or the lender, not both, and RESPA bans referral fees. Locks are written and cover the closing, applications stay honest, and only a written commitment satisfies a mortgage contingency.

questions.q: A company that arranges loans between borrowers and lenders but does not fund the loans with its own money is a:
c: Mortgage broker
Mortgage banker
Savings bank
Secondary market investor
questions.x: A mortgage broker arranges loans that lenders fund. Mortgage banker is the trap: a banker lends its own funds and closes in its own name.

questions.q: A mortgage banker differs from a mortgage broker because the mortgage banker:
c: Arranges commercial loans exclusively
Funds loans with its own money
Cannot sell loans to investors
Is regulated by the DOS
questions.x: Mortgage bankers fund loans, often with warehouse lines, and usually sell them on the secondary market. DOS is the trap: both brokers and bankers are regulated by DFS.

questions.q: In New York, mortgage brokers and mortgage bankers are regulated by the:
c: Department of State
Dept. of Housing and Urban Development
Department of Financial Services
Attorney General's office
questions.x: DFS registers mortgage brokers and licenses mortgage bankers and loan originators. Department of State is the trap: it licenses real estate brokers and salespersons, not mortgage firms.

questions.q: An individual who takes residential mortgage applications and negotiates loan terms for compensation generally needs a license as a:
c: Real estate associate broker
Certified appraiser
Notary public
Mortgage loan originator
questions.x: The SAFE Act and NY Banking Law require individual loan originators to be licensed and registered through NMLS. The real estate license is the trap: it does not cover taking loan applications.

questions.q: A real estate brokerage that lists a home also arranges the buyer's mortgage as a mortgage broker in the same deal. New York requires:
c: A mortgage broker dual agency disclosure
The RPL 443 agency disclosure form
Written approval from HUD
No added disclosure
questions.x: NY banking regulations (3 NYCRR 38.12) require a mortgage broker dual agency disclosure, signed before mortgage brokerage services begin. RPL 443 is the trap: that form covers real estate agency, not the mortgage role.

questions.q: An estimate of how much a buyer may be able to borrow, based on unverified information the buyer provides, is a:
c: Conditional commitment
Prequalification
Preapproval
Rate lock
questions.x: Prequalification relies on what the buyer says, with no documents verified. Preapproval is the trap: it involves a credit pull and document review.

questions.q: Which is the strongest evidence of financing for a specific property?
c: Prequalification letter
Preapproval letter
Mortgage commitment
Loan application
questions.x: A commitment is issued after underwriting and appraisal for a specific property. Preapproval is the trap: it verifies the buyer but is issued before a property is chosen.

questions.q: A lender's written guarantee of a specific interest rate and points for a stated period is a:
c: Buydown
Commitment
Lender rebate
Rate lock
questions.x: A rate lock holds a rate and points until an expiration date. Commitment is the trap: it is the promise to make the loan, which may or may not include a locked rate.

questions.q: The process in which a lender evaluates a borrower's credit, capacity, capital, and the collateral to decide whether to make a loan is:
c: Underwriting
Origination
Servicing
Securitization
questions.x: Underwriting is the risk evaluation. Origination is the trap: it is taking and processing the application, which comes before the underwriter's decision.

questions.q: A loan that exceeds Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac loan limits or does not meet their underwriting standards is a:
c: Conforming loan
Nonconforming loan
Government loan
Purchase money loan
questions.x: Nonconforming loans, such as jumbos, cannot be sold to Fannie or Freddie. Government loan is the trap: FHA and VA loans follow their own agency rules, which is a separate category.

questions.q: A borrower accepts a rate 0.25% above the lowest available, and the lender pays $3,500 that is credited toward the borrower's closing costs. This is best described as a:
c: Discount point
Kickback
Lender rebate
Prepayment penalty
questions.x: A lender rebate (lender credit) is money from the lender in exchange for a higher rate. Discount points are the trap: they work in reverse, with the borrower paying to lower the rate.

questions.q: Before accepting any fee from a borrower, a New York mortgage broker provides the:
c: Closing Disclosure
Mortgage commitment
RPL 443 agency disclosure
Pre-application fee agreement
questions.x: The pre-application disclosure and fee agreement explains the broker's role, fees, and refund terms before any fee is taken. The Closing Disclosure is the trap: it comes at the end of the process.

questions.q: Under federal loan originator compensation rules, a mortgage broker in a single transaction may be paid by:
c: Borrower or lender, not both
More for a higher interest rate
A referral fee from the agent
Both sides, if disclosed
questions.x: Federal rules bar dual compensation and pay that varies with loan terms. Both sides if disclosed is the trap: disclosure does not cure dual compensation.

questions.q: A mortgage broker typically does each of the following EXCEPT:
c: Take the borrower's application
Fund the loan with its own money
Shop the file to several lenders
Help gather underwriting papers
questions.x: Funding is what a lender or mortgage banker does. Gathering documents is the trap: it sounds like lender work, but brokers routinely shepherd the file through underwriting.

questions.q: A buyer's preapproval letter is dated before she found the house. The seller's attorney asks whether the mortgage contingency is satisfied. The correct answer is:
c: Yes, preapproval satisfies it
Yes, if her credit is strong
No; a commitment is required
No, it needs a closed loan
questions.x: Preapproval does not cover this property or its appraisal; the written commitment does, and that is what contingency clauses require. The closed loan is the trap: the contingency is met before closing, by the commitment.

questions.q: A mortgage broker offers a real estate salesperson $300 for each buyer she refers. The salesperson should:
c: Accept if disclosed to the buyer
Accept if it is paid through her broker
Accept if under $500
Decline; RESPA bars referral fees
questions.x: RESPA Section 8 bans kickbacks and referral fees for settlement services. Paying through her broker is the trap: routing a kickback through the broker does not make it legal.

questions.q: A rate lock-in agreement in New York should:
c: Be written, stating its terms
Be oral so it can be adjusted later
Last for the full life of the loan
Be given after the closing
questions.x: Lock-ins are written and state the rate, points, and expiration. Life of the loan is the trap: a lock covers a period before closing, not the loan term.

questions.q: Which document is issued after a lender has verified credit and income but before a specific property has been chosen?
c: Commitment
Preapproval
Closing Disclosure
Satisfaction
questions.x: Preapproval verifies the borrower but not a property. Commitment is the trap: it requires the property and its appraisal.

questions.q: An underwriter evaluates each of the following EXCEPT:
c: The borrower's credit history
The borrower's debt ratios
The borrower's religion
The property's appraised value
questions.x: Religion is a protected basis under ECOA and the Fair Housing Act. The appraisal is the trap for anyone who thinks underwriting is only about the borrower: collateral is a core factor.

questions.q: A borrower locked a rate for 30 days, but the co-op board interview pushes closing to day 45. The most likely result is:
c: The rate is guaranteed until closing
The lender has to lower the rate
The commitment becomes a preapproval
She may pay to extend the lock
questions.x: When a lock expires, the borrower generally pays an extension fee or floats to the current market rate. The guarantee until closing is the trap: locks are not open-ended.

questions.q: A $1.6 million loan on a one-unit Manhattan condo in 2026 is most likely a:
c: Jumbo loan
Conforming high-cost loan
FHA-insured loan
SONYMA first-time loan
questions.x: The 2026 high-cost conforming limit for one unit is $1,249,125, so $1.6 million is a jumbo, nonconforming loan. Conforming high-cost is the trap: the higher NYC-area limit still tops out below $1.6 million.

questions.q: The mortgage broker dual agency disclosure explains each of the following EXCEPT:
c: That the firm acts in a dual capacity
The borrower's rights in dual agency
The seller's lowest acceptable price
Whether it uses three or fewer lenders
questions.x: The disclosure covers the dual role, the borrower's rights, and the lender count. The lender count is the trap: it seems like a business detail, but it is part of the form. A seller's bottom line stays confidential.

questions.q: A mortgage commitment typically:
c: Has no conditions attached
Is issued before the property appraisal
Equals a prequalification
Has conditions and an expiration
questions.x: Commitments list conditions to clear before closing and expire on a date. No conditions is the trap: even a commitment is conditional until those items are cleared.

questions.q: A licensed real estate salesperson tells a buyer, "I'll broker your mortgage too; my real estate license covers it." This statement is:
c: Correct; both are real estate services
Incorrect; that needs DFS licensing
Correct, if her broker approves
Incorrect; banks alone arrange loans
questions.x: Real estate licenses come from DOS; mortgage brokering requires DFS registration and licensed loan originators. Banks alone is the trap: non-bank mortgage brokers and bankers are lawful when licensed.

questions.q: A loan that meets Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac size limits and underwriting guidelines is called a:
c: Jumbo loan
Subprime loan
Conforming loan
Nonconforming loan
questions.x: Conforming loans can be sold to Fannie and Freddie. Jumbo is the trap: jumbo loans exceed the size limit, which makes them nonconforming.

questions.q: A firm represents both buyer and seller as real estate broker and also arranges the buyer's loan as mortgage broker. Which disclosures does it need?
c: The RPL 443 form, which covers both roles
The mortgage broker form, which covers both roles
Both the RPL 443 and Banking Law forms
Neither, if the buyer pays no fee to the firm
questions.x: RPL 443 dual agency (one real estate broker for buyer and seller) and Banking Law dual agency (one firm as real estate broker and mortgage broker) are separate, so a firm doing both can need both disclosures. The trap is thinking one form covers both roles.

questions.q: The mortgage broker dual agency disclosure under NY Banking regulations addresses a firm that is:
c: Both the real estate broker and the mortgage broker
One real estate broker acting for both buyer and seller
A mortgage banker funding its own loans
A lender that sells loans on the secondary market
questions.x: The Banking Law dual agency disclosure covers one firm acting as real estate broker and mortgage broker in the same deal. Acting for both buyer and seller is the trap: that is RPL 443 real estate dual agency, a separate disclosure.

questions.concept: Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure timing
questions.q: The borrower must receive the Loan Estimate:
c: 3 business days before the closing
10 business days after the application
30 days after the application
3 business days after the application
questions.x: The Loan Estimate is due within 3 business days of the application. "3 business days before closing" is the trap: that is the Closing Disclosure deadline.

questions.concept: Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure timing
questions.q: When must the borrower receive the Closing Disclosure?
c: Within 3 business days of the application
At least 3 business days before closing
At the closing table, with the deed
10 days after the rate lock is signed
questions.x: The Closing Disclosure arrives 3 business days before closing. "Within 3 business days of the application" is the trap: that is the Loan Estimate deadline.

questions.q: Why might a self-employed buyer with nontraditional income records benefit from a mortgage broker?
c: Brokers can approve loans that banks have rejected
Brokers know which lenders hold such loans
Brokers fund nonconforming loans with their own money
Brokers are exempt from income verification rules
questions.x: Nonconforming loans, such as for a self-employed borrower with nontraditional documents, are where brokers earn their keep: they know which lenders keep such loans in portfolio. Funding the loan is the trap: a broker arranges loans but does not fund them.

questions.q: Which borrower's loan is most likely nonconforming even though it is under the size limit?
c: A salaried nurse with two years of W-2s and strong credit
A buyer with steady pay and a 20% down payment
A teacher whose loan meets Fannie Mae's guidelines
A self-employed buyer with nontraditional income papers
questions.x: A loan can be nonconforming without being a jumbo when the borrower's documentation does not fit Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac rules, as with nontraditional self-employed income. The 20% down payment is the trap: down payment size alone does not make a loan nonconforming.

questions.q: Which statement describes a mortgage broker?
c: It funds loans from a warehouse line
It services loans after closing
It guarantees mortgage securities
It arranges loans others fund
questions.x: A mortgage broker arranges loans that a lender funds. The warehouse line is the trap: that is how a mortgage banker funds its own loans.

questions.q: A company closes loans in its own name using a warehouse line of credit, then sells them to Fannie Mae. It is a:
c: Mortgage banker
Mortgage broker
Loan servicer
Individual loan originator
questions.x: Funding and closing in its own name makes it a mortgage banker. Mortgage broker is the trap: selling to Fannie Mae does not change who funded the loan.

questions.q: A consumer has a complaint about a New York mortgage banker. Which agency regulates it?
c: The Department of State (DOS)
Financial Services (DFS)
HUD's FHA office
The county clerk
questions.x: The Department of Financial Services licenses and supervises mortgage bankers. DOS is the trap: it handles real estate licensees, not mortgage firms.

questions.q: Diane, a licensed real estate salesperson, wants to take mortgage applications for a lender. She needs:
c: Nothing beyond her DOS license
An associate broker license
An MLO license through NMLS
A notary commission
questions.x: Taking applications for compensation requires a mortgage loan originator license through NMLS. The associate broker license is the trap: any DOS license is a real estate license, not a lending license.

questions.q: When does a firm acting as both real estate broker and mortgage broker deliver the mortgage broker dual agency disclosure?
c: At the closing table
After the commitment issues
With the Loan Estimate
Before services begin
questions.x: It is signed before mortgage brokerage services begin. The Loan Estimate is the trap: that federal form comes after the application, too late for this disclosure.

questions.q: A buyer talks with a loan officer for ten minutes and gets a letter estimating she can borrow $500,000. No documents were checked. She has a:
c: Prequalification
Preapproval
Commitment
Conditional approval
questions.x: An estimate based on the buyer's own unverified statements is a prequalification. Preapproval is the trap: it requires a credit pull and document review.

questions.q: Two buyers make equal offers on a Ditmas Park co-op. Which financing document is strongest?
c: A preapproval letter
A mortgage commitment
A prequalification letter
A completed application
questions.x: A commitment follows underwriting and appraisal of the specific property. Preapproval is the trap: it is strong evidence of creditworthiness but not tied to this unit.

questions.q: A borrower wants protection in case rates rise before her closing in 45 days. She should get:
c: A buydown
A commitment
A rate lock
A lender credit
questions.x: A rate lock holds the rate and points for a stated period. Commitment is the trap: a commitment promises the loan but may leave the rate floating.

questions.q: An underwriter reviewing a mortgage file focuses on:
c: Marketing the loan to investors
Collecting the monthly payments
Taking the initial application
Credit, capacity, and collateral
questions.x: Underwriting evaluates credit, capacity, capital, and collateral. Collecting payments is the trap: that is servicing, after closing.

questions.q: A $2 million loan on a Westchester house exceeds the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac limit. It is:
c: Nonconforming
Conforming
Government-backed
Subprime by law
questions.x: Exceeding the agency limit makes it nonconforming (a jumbo). Subprime is the trap: subprime describes the borrower's credit, not the loan size.

questions.q: A borrower pays the lender extra at closing to get a lower rate, the reverse of a lender rebate. This payment is called:
c: A lender credit
Discount points
A rate lock extension
A yield spread
questions.x: Discount points buy the rate down. Lender credit is the trap: that is the rebate itself, money from the lender for a higher rate.

questions.q: A New York mortgage broker asks for a $500 fee at the first meeting. Before taking it, the broker should provide:
c: The Closing Disclosure
The RPL 443 agency disclosure
A pre-application disclosure
A mortgage commitment
questions.x: The pre-application disclosure and fee agreement comes before any fee. RPL 443 is the trap: it governs real estate agency, not mortgage broker fees.

questions.q: A mortgage broker is paid 1% of the loan by the lender. Under federal compensation rules, which is true?
c: It may also bill the borrower
Its pay may rise with the rate
It may split pay with agents
It can't bill the borrower too
questions.x: A broker may be paid by the lender or the borrower in a transaction, not both. Billing the borrower is the trap: disclosure does not permit dual compensation.

questions.q: Which task belongs to a mortgage banker but not to a mortgage broker?
c: Funding the loan at closing
Taking the application
Pulling the credit report
Collecting the income documents
questions.x: Only the banker funds with its own money. Pulling credit is the trap: brokers do that too while preparing the file.

questions.q: A buyer's contract has a mortgage contingency. Which document normally satisfies it?
c: A preapproval letter
A written commitment
A Loan Estimate
A rate lock letter
questions.x: A written mortgage commitment for this property satisfies the contingency. The rate lock is the trap: it protects the rate but is not a promise to lend.

questions.q: A title agency offers a salesperson a $100 gift card for each client she sends. Under RESPA this is:
c: Legal if disclosed
Legal under $500
A banned referral fee
Legal if paid to her broker
questions.x: Anything of value for referring settlement business is a prohibited kickback. Legal if disclosed is the trap: disclosure does not cure a Section 8 violation.

questions.q: A loan officer tells a borrower by phone, "You're locked at 6.1%." Nothing is put in writing. In New York this lock is:
c: Binding for 60 days
Binding until closing
Binding if recorded
Not properly documented
questions.x: NY lock-ins are written and state the rate, points, and expiration. Binding through closing is the trap: no lock is open-ended, written or not.

questions.q: A lender pulled credit and verified a buyer's income and assets, but she has not chosen a house. She holds a:
c: Preapproval
Commitment
Prequalification
Closing Disclosure
questions.x: Verified borrower, no property yet: preapproval. Prequalification is the trap: it involves no verification.

questions.q: An underwriter may properly consider which of these?
c: The borrower's national origin
The borrower's debt-to-income ratio
The borrower's familial status
The racial makeup of the neighborhood
questions.x: Capacity, measured by debt ratios, is a core underwriting factor. Neighborhood racial makeup is the trap: basing loans on it is redlining.

questions.q: A 45-day rate lock expires May 10, and closing moves to May 20. The borrower's options usually include:
c: A free automatic extension
A demand that the lender lower the rate
Paying to extend or floating to market
Cancelling the commitment for a refund
questions.x: An expired lock means paying an extension fee or taking the current market rate. The free extension is the trap: extensions are usually charged.

questions.q: The 2026 high-cost-area conforming limit for a one-unit home is $1,249,125. A $1.1 million loan on a Brooklyn condo that meets agency guidelines is:
c: A jumbo loan
An FHA loan
A nonconforming jumbo
A conforming loan
questions.x: $1.1 million is under the high-cost limit, so the loan can be conforming. Jumbo is the trap: a large loan is not automatically a jumbo in a high-cost area.

questions.q: The mortgage broker dual agency disclosure is signed by:
c: The borrower and the seller
The borrower and the lender
The buyer's attorney alone
The seller and the listing agent
questions.x: Both the borrower and the seller sign, since the firm's dual role affects both. The lender is the trap: the lender is not a party to this disclosure.

questions.q: A buyer's commitment letter says "subject to receipt of final pay stubs; expires June 30." This is:
c: Unusual; commitments are final
Typical of a commitment
A sign it is a preapproval
A prequalification in disguise
questions.x: Commitments normally carry conditions and an expiration date. Unusual is the trap: unconditional commitments are rare.

questions.q: Which party may lawfully arrange a buyer's mortgage for a fee in New York?
c: A DOS salesperson, through her broker
Any licensed real estate broker
A DFS-registered mortgage broker
An attorney's paralegal
questions.x: Mortgage brokering requires DFS registration with licensed loan originators. The real estate broker is the trap: a DOS license does not authorize mortgage brokering.

questions.q: Which feature makes a loan conforming?
c: It meets Fannie and Freddie rules
It is insured by the FHA or VA
It has a fixed 30-year rate
It exceeds the agency loan limit
questions.x: Conforming means it meets Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac size and underwriting rules. FHA insurance is the trap: government loans follow their own agency rules.

questions.concept: Real estate licensee as mortgage broker
questions.q: A real estate broker starts charging buyers $750 to arrange their mortgage loans. Under the Banking Law, the broker:
c: Is exempt as a licensed real estate broker
Needs only a DOS license amendment
May charge it if the buyer signs a waiver
Must register with DFS
questions.x: Banking Law 590 exempts a real estate licensee only if no fee is taken for mortgage services. Once the broker charges for arranging loans, DFS registration is required, and individuals taking applications need MLO licenses. The exemption choice is the trap: it exists, but the fee removes it.

questions.concept: Real estate licensee as mortgage broker
questions.q: A salesperson gives buyers a list of local lenders and explains how points work, without any compensation. This activity:
c: Is not mortgage brokering
Requires DFS mortgage broker registration
Requires an MLO license from NMLS
Is a RESPA violation
questions.x: A real estate licensee who accepts no fee, directly or indirectly, for mortgage help is not treated as a mortgage broker under Banking Law 590. The MLO choice is the trap: originator licensing applies to people taking applications or negotiating terms for compensation in the mortgage business.

questions.q: A firm is the listing broker and will also act as mortgage broker for the buyer of that listing. The required DFS dual agency disclosure must be signed by:
c: The buyer alone
The lender and the buyer
Both buyer and seller
The seller alone
questions.x: Under 3 NYCRR 38.12 the disclosure goes to both the buyer/borrower and the seller at first substantive contact, and both must sign before mortgage brokerage services are provided. The buyer-alone choice is the trap: the seller is the firm's real estate client and also gives up undivided loyalty.

questions.q: The NY mortgage broker dual agency disclosure includes all of the following EXCEPT:
c: Whether the broker uses three or fewer lenders
That each party gives up undivided loyalty
That each party may hire its own broker
The interest rate the buyer will receive
questions.x: The disclosure explains the dual role, the loss of undivided loyalty, each side's right to separate representation, and whether the broker places loans with three or fewer lenders. It does not set or quote a rate. The three-lenders item is the tempting wrong pick, but it is a required checkbox on the form.

questions.q: A mortgage broker will be paid 1% by the lender on a loan. The broker may also:
c: Charge the borrower a broker fee if disclosed
Raise its fee if the borrower takes a higher rate
Pass through actual third-party costs
Charge the borrower a processing fee as its pay
questions.x: Under the federal loan originator compensation rules, a broker paid by the lender may not also take compensation from the borrower, and pay may not vary with the rate. Actual third-party costs are not broker compensation. The disclosed-fee choice is the trap: disclosure does not cure dual compensation.

questions.q: Under federal loan originator compensation rules, a mortgage broker's pay on a loan may NOT vary based on:
c: The loan amount
The loan's interest rate
Whether the lender or borrower pays
The broker's written fee agreement
questions.x: Originator pay can be a percentage of the loan amount, but it may not vary with the loan's rate or other terms, which removes the incentive to steer borrowers into costlier loans. Loan amount is the trap: a percentage-of-loan fee is allowed.

questions.q: A borrower needs a $600,000 loan, well under the conforming limit, but documents income with 12 months of bank statements instead of tax returns. Her loan is most likely:
c: Nonconforming, due to the income records
Conforming, since it is under the limit
An FHA loan, by default
A jumbo loan, because of the documentation
questions.x: Conforming loans must meet Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac underwriting rules as well as size limits. Bank-statement income does not fit those rules, so a portfolio lender's nonconforming loan is likely. The jumbo choice is the trap: jumbo means above the size limit, which this loan is not.

questions.q: A conforming loan is one that:
c: Meets Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac standards
Is insured by FHA or guaranteed by VA
Is made by a bank rather than a mortgage broker
Has a fixed rate for at least 15 years
questions.x: Conforming means the loan fits the standards set for purchase by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, both on size and on underwriting. FHA and VA are the trap: those are government-backed loans with their own rules, sold through Ginnie Mae securities.

questions.q: A buyer pays 1.5 points on a $480,000 loan for a $600,000 home. The points cost:
questions.x: A point is 1% of the loan amount: 1.5% x $480,000 = $7,200. The $9,000 trap is 1.5% of the $600,000 price; points are always figured on the loan, not the purchase price.

questions.q: A lender charges $6,300 in discount points on a $420,000 loan. How many points is that?
c: 1 point
2 points
1.5 points
0.15 points
questions.x: $6,300 / $420,000 = 0.015, or 1.5 points, since each point is 1% of the loan. The 0.15 trap comes from misplacing the decimal when converting 0.015 to points.

questions.q: A buyer's 30-day rate lock expires before a delayed closing, and market rates have risen. The buyer's usual choices are:
c: Close at the old rate, since a lock survives delays
Cancel under the mortgage contingency at no cost
Demand the seller pay the higher rate
Pay to extend, or relock at market
questions.x: A lock guarantees a rate only for its stated period. If closing slips past it, the borrower typically pays an extension fee or relocks at market. The contingency choice is the trap: in most contracts the contingency is satisfied once a commitment issues, and an expired lock is not a commitment failure.

questions.q: A rate lock is best described as:
c: A cap on how high an adjustable rate can rise
A promise to make a loan on a specific property
A guaranteed rate and points for a set time
A borrower's agreement not to shop other lenders
questions.x: A rate lock guarantees a stated rate and points until its expiration date, sometimes for a fee. The specific-property promise is the trap: that is the mortgage commitment, a separate document with its own expiration.

cram.html: Mortgage broker arranges, does not fund. Mortgage banker funds with its own money.
NY regulator for mortgage brokers, bankers, and originators: DFS, not DOS.
Brokers register with DFS; bankers are licensed by DFS (Banking Law Article 12-D).
Individual loan originators need an MLO license through NMLS (SAFE Act).
Real estate broker also acting as mortgage broker in the same deal: mortgage broker dual agency disclosure, signed by borrower and seller before services.
Banking Law dual agency is separate from RPL 443 dual agency.
Pre-application disclosure and fee agreement: signed before the broker takes any fee.
Strength: prequalification (unverified) < preapproval (verified borrower) < commitment (specific property).
Only a written commitment satisfies a mortgage contingency.
Rate lock: in writing, rate, points, expiration. Lock past the expected closing date.
Lender rebate = higher rate, lender pays. Discount points = borrower pays, lower rate.
Broker may be paid by borrower or lender, not both; pay cannot vary with the rate.
Referral fees from lenders to real estate licensees: banned by RESPA, even if disclosed.
2026 conforming limit: $832,750 baseline, up to $1,249,125 in high-cost areas. Above = jumbo, nonconforming.
Underwriting reviews credit, capacity, capital, collateral.

subjects.title: Property Management
subjects.blurb: Property managers are general agents who run buildings for owners. The exam tests when a license is required, what goes in the management agreement, budgets, and maintenance types.

lessons.title: The Manager, the License, and the Agreement
lessons.tagline: A property manager runs someone else's building as if it were their own, and owes the owner loyalty to prove it.
objectives: Describe what property managers do and the kinds of property they manage
Decide when a property manager needs a NY license, and apply the resident manager exception
Explain why the management agreement creates a general agency and list what it should contain
Compare office, retail, residential, and condo/co-op management
Name the main professional designations

blocks.title: Astoria, 31st Avenue
blocks.html: Sal Russo is 71 and tired of answering 2 am calls about the boiler. "Jordan, you manage it. Collect the rents, find tenants, fix stuff. I'll give you 5% of what comes in. Handshake, like the old days." Jordan is flattered. What has to happen before Jordan touches a single rent check?
blocks.casual: Sal Russo is 71 and done with 2 am boiler calls. "Jordan, you manage it. Collect the rents, find tenants, fix stuff. I'll give you 5% of what comes in. Handshake, like the old days." Jordan's flattered. But what has to happen before Jordan touches a single rent check?

deeper.plain: Managing someone else's building for pay is licensed work, and it has to run through the broker with a written agreement.
deeper.picture: It's like being handed the keys to someone's restaurant. Before you open the register, there needs to be a contract, a bank account, and the right permit on the wall.
deeper.street: Sal's six units bring in about $15,000 a month. Jordan's 5% would be $750. Diane tells Jordan the agreement has to be between Sal and Hudson & Hart, in writing, with rents and deposits going into firm accounts.
deeper.stakes: A handshake deal paid straight to Jordan breaks the rule that salespersons are paid only by their broker. If money goes missing, nobody can show who agreed to what.
deeper.exam: Scenarios with "handshake" and "collect rents" are testing that rent collection for others needs a license and that a salesperson works through the broker.

blocks.html: Property management is operating real estate for an owner to meet the owner's goals: usually the best net income over time while protecting the asset's value. A property manager does what an owner would do if the owner had the time and skill.
blocks.casual: Property management means running real estate for an owner to hit the owner's goals: usually the best net income over time while protecting what the building's worth. A property manager does what the owner would do, if the owner had the time and the know-how.

deeper.plain: A manager runs the building the way a skilled owner would, aiming for steady income and a building that holds its value.
deeper.picture: A property manager is a hired captain. The owner owns the ship and sets the destination; the captain sails it day to day.
deeper.street: Evelyn owns a Downtown Brooklyn office building and wants long-term value, not a quick buck. Her manager spends on a new roof now, even though it cuts this year's income, because that's Evelyn's goal.
deeper.stakes: A manager who squeezes income by skipping maintenance can wreck the building's value and the owner's real goal.
deeper.exam: The manager's primary aim is the owner's objectives, usually maximizing net income while preserving value.

items: Marketing and leasing: advertise, show, screen, negotiate, and sign leases
Collecting rent and handling security deposits
Tenant relations: complaints, renewals, enforcement, evictions
Maintenance: hire and supervise staff and contractors, inspect, plan capital work
Accounting and reporting: budgets, rent rolls, monthly and annual reports
Compliance: building codes, fair housing, rent regulation, registrations
Risk management and insurance
blocks.casual: What the job covers: marketing and leasing (advertise, show, screen, negotiate, sign leases); collecting rent and handling security deposits; tenant relations (complaints, renewals, enforcement, evictions); maintenance (hire and supervise staff and contractors, inspect, plan capital work); accounting and reporting (budgets, rent rolls, monthly and annual reports); compliance (building codes, fair housing, rent regulation, registrations); and risk management and insurance.

deeper.plain: A manager handles leasing, money, tenants, repairs, books, rules and insurance.
deeper.picture: Seven hats on one hook: leasing agent, cashier, counselor, maintenance boss, bookkeeper, compliance cop, insurance planner.
deeper.street: In one week managing Sal's building, Jordan's firm shows a vacant unit, deposits rents, calms a tenant about noise, books a plumber, sends Sal a monthly report, files the HPD registration and checks the liability policy.
deeper.stakes: Drop any one hat and something breaks: missed registrations bring fines, weak screening brings fair housing risk, bad books bring owner lawsuits.
deeper.exam: Expect a "which is NOT a typical manager function" question. Watch for answers like "giving tax advice" or "performing appraisals."

blocks.html: In New York, collecting rent or leasing space for another person, for a fee, is brokerage under RPL 440. An independent property manager or management company needs a broker license, and its salespersons need licenses too. Jordan, a salesperson, cannot sign Sal up personally: the management agreement must be with Hudson & Hart, and the fee goes to the firm.
blocks.casual: In New York, collecting rent or leasing space for someone else, for a fee, is brokerage under RPL 440. An independent property manager or management company needs a broker license, and its salespersons need licenses too. Jordan's a salesperson, so Jordan can't sign Sal up personally. The management agreement has to be with Hudson & Hart, and the fee goes to the firm.

deeper.plain: Managing rentals for pay is real estate brokerage, so the firm needs a broker license and the contract is with the firm.
deeper.picture: Jordan is a player on Hudson & Hart's team. The team signs the deal, the team gets paid, and Jordan gets a cut from the team.
deeper.street: Sal signs a management agreement with Hudson & Hart at 5% of collected rents. Diane's firm receives the $750 a month and pays Jordan's share per their contract.
deeper.stakes: If Jordan takes the fee directly, it's a violation for Jordan and a supervision problem for Diane, and Sal has no real firm standing behind the deal.
deeper.exam: Property management for others for a fee needs a broker license. Salespersons can do it only under a sponsoring broker.

left.title: License needed
items: A management company collecting rents for several owners
A salesperson leasing apartments for a landlord client
A manager paid a percentage of rents who negotiates leases

right.title: No license needed
items: The owner managing her own building
A resident manager or superintendent employed by the owner, managing that owner's building
Clerical staff who do not lease or negotiate

deeper.plain: If you're managing someone else's property for a fee, you need a license. If you're the owner or the owner's own on-site employee, you don't.
deeper.picture: Ask: whose building is it, and who signs your paycheck? If both answers are the same owner and you live on site, you're covered by the owner's exemption.
deeper.street: Kim's co-op on the Upper West Side hires a management company: licensed. The building's live-in super, employed by the co-op, handles daily issues: no license needed. A Hudson & Hart salesperson leasing units for a landlord client: licensed, under Diane.
deeper.stakes: Misreading this line is how unlicensed managers end up collecting rents and owners end up exposed.
deeper.exam: Owner, owner's resident manager, clerical staff: no license. Management company or salesperson leasing for a landlord: license required.

blocks.html: The resident manager exception rests on the owner's own exemption: a salaried employee of the owner, living on site and working only for that owner, acts as the owner rather than as a broker for others. Once the resident manager starts collecting rents for a second owner for a fee, the exception is gone.
blocks.casual: The resident manager exception piggybacks on the owner's own exemption. A salaried employee of the owner, living on site and working only for that owner, is acting as the owner, not as a broker for others. The moment that person starts collecting rents for a second owner for a fee, the exception's gone.

deeper.plain: An on-site manager working for one owner borrows that owner's exemption. Working for a second owner breaks it.
deeper.picture: It's like a family member using a household membership card. It works for that household only.
deeper.street: Sal's longtime super, Hector, lives in unit 1A and collects rents for Sal on salary. Fine. The owner next door offers Hector $200 a month to collect his rents too. Now Hector is acting for a second owner for a fee and needs a license.
deeper.stakes: Supers drift into licensed work all the time. The owners and the super can get caught in an unlicensed activity complaint.
deeper.exam: Key words: salaried, employed by the owner, one owner, on site. Add a second owner or a fee per deal and the exemption fails.

blocks.title: Commission-paid supers
blocks.html: A super who gets $300 per apartment rented from an outside management firm is not the owner's employee and is being paid per transaction. That is a licensed activity done by an unlicensed person.
blocks.casual: Watch out for this one. A super who gets $300 for every apartment rented from an outside management firm isn't the owner's employee, and he's being paid per deal. That's licensed activity done by someone with no license.

deeper.plain: Per-deal pay from an outside firm turns the super into an unlicensed agent.
deeper.picture: It's a tip jar for each lease signed. Once there's a tip jar per deal, the State sees a broker, not a super.
deeper.street: A Washington Heights management company pays a super $300 every time a tenant he shows signs a lease. Over a year he rents 15 units and pockets $4,500. A tenant files a complaint, and DOS looks at the firm for paying an unlicensed person.
deeper.stakes: The firm can be fined for paying unlicensed people, and the super faces unlicensed activity penalties.
deeper.exam: Two red flags together: not the owner's employee, and paid per transaction. The answer is licensed activity by an unlicensed person.

blocks.q: Which person most clearly needs a real estate broker license?
c: A super employed by one owner, living in the building, who collects rent there
An owner managing her own 4-family in Ridgewood
A company that collects rent and signs leases for 30 owners for a percentage fee
A bookkeeper who reconciles the rent account for a licensed manager
blocks.x: Collecting rent and leasing for others for a fee requires a broker license. The owner and her resident employee are covered by the owner exemption; the bookkeeper does clerical work.

blocks.html: The management agreement is the employment contract between owner and manager. It creates an agency in which the manager is a general agent: authorized to handle a range of ongoing matters for one principal, not just one task. As a fiduciary, the manager owes the owner all the agency duties: obedience, loyalty, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting, and reasonable care.
blocks.casual: The management agreement is the employment contract between the owner and the manager. It makes the manager a general agent: someone authorized to handle a whole range of ongoing matters for one principal, not just one task. And as a fiduciary, the manager owes the owner every agency duty: obedience, loyalty, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting, and reasonable care.

deeper.plain: The manager is the owner's ongoing agent with full fiduciary duties.
deeper.picture: A listing agent is hired for one errand. A property manager is handed the household checkbook and the keys for the long haul.
deeper.street: Hudson & Hart manages Sal's building. A contractor offers Diane's firm a quiet 10% kickback for steering work to him. Loyalty and disclosure mean the firm either refuses or tells Sal and gets his consent; secret profits are out.
deeper.stakes: A manager who takes hidden payments or hides problems breaches fiduciary duty and can be sued by the owner and disciplined by DOS.
deeper.exam: Property manager = general agent. Duties = OLD CAR. The management agreement creates the agency.

blocks.title: General vs special
blocks.html: A listing broker is a special agent (one task: sell this house). A property manager is a general agent (run the building). Power of attorney for everything would be a universal agent.
blocks.casual: General versus special: a listing broker is a special agent (one task: sell this house). A property manager is a general agent (run the building). Power of attorney covering everything would make someone a universal agent.

deeper.plain: Special = one job. General = a range of ongoing jobs. Universal = everything.
deeper.picture: Special agent is a plumber called for one leak. General agent is the building's full-time super. Universal agent is someone holding your power of attorney for your whole life's business.
deeper.street: The Okafors hire Hudson & Hart to sell the brownstone: special agency. Sal hires Hudson & Hart to run 31st Avenue: general agency. Neither gives Diane power to sell Sal's car.
deeper.stakes: Agents who act beyond their authority can bind no one and get sued for overstepping.
deeper.exam: Classic pairing: listing broker = special, property manager = general. Universal needs a broad power of attorney.

blocks.html: It should be written and signed (and must be if it runs longer than a year, under the statute of frauds). Typical contents:
blocks.casual: Put it in writing and sign it. If it runs longer than a year, the statute of frauds says it has to be. Here's what usually goes in it:

deeper.plain: A written, signed contract protects both owner and manager, and it's required by law if longer than a year.
deeper.picture: A handshake is a sticky note. A management agreement is the building's operating manual with both signatures on page one.
deeper.street: Sal wants a three-year deal. Under the statute of frauds, that must be in writing. Diane drafts it, both sign, and Sal gets a copy that day.
deeper.stakes: Without writing, a fee dispute turns into "he said, she said," and a contract over a year may be unenforceable.
deeper.exam: Statute of frauds: agreements that can't be performed within a year must be in writing. A management agreement over a year counts.

head: Clause
What it settles
rows: What the manager may do without asking: lease terms, repair spending limit, hiring
What reports, how often (monthly statement, annual budget)
Usually a percentage of collected rents, sometimes plus leasing fees or a flat minimum
Bank accounts, escrow for deposits, who pays bills
Required coverage; manager named as additional insured
Owner funds shortfalls; owner's goals (income, appreciation, condition)
How and why either side can end it, notice period

deeper.plain: The agreement nails down what's managed, for how long, what the manager can do alone, how the money flows, and how to end it.
deeper.picture: Think of it as the building's rulebook for two players: what each one does, how they score, and how either can leave the game.
deeper.street: Sal's agreement lets Hudson & Hart approve repairs up to $2,500 without calling him, pays 5% of collected rents, requires a monthly statement by the 15th, names the firm as additional insured, and allows either side to end it on 60 days' notice.
deeper.stakes: Leave out the repair limit and the manager either bothers the owner over every drip or spends money the owner never approved.
deeper.exam: Fee is usually a percentage of collected rents, not scheduled rents. Know the main clauses: authority, reporting, fee, accounting, insurance, termination.

blocks.title: Deposits are still escrow
blocks.html: Tenant security deposits are the tenant's money. A manager holds them in a separate account, never mixed with the owner's operating funds or the manager's own. In buildings with 6 or more units, deposits must be in an interest-bearing account, with interest going to the tenant (the landlord may keep 1% a year as an administrative fee).
blocks.casual: Deposits are still escrow. A tenant's security deposit is the tenant's money. The manager keeps it in a separate account, never mixed with the owner's operating money or the manager's own. In buildings with 6 or more units, deposits have to sit in an interest-bearing account with the interest going to the tenant (the landlord can keep 1% a year as an admin fee).

deeper.plain: Security deposits belong to the tenant, so they stay separate, and in bigger buildings they earn interest for the tenant.
deeper.picture: It's a locked box with the tenant's name on it, sitting in the manager's office. Nobody gets to borrow from it.
deeper.street: Sal's six-unit building has $15,000 in deposits. Since it's 6 or more units, the money sits in an interest-bearing account. If it earns 3%, about $450 a year, Sal can keep 1% of the deposits ($150) as his fee and the rest belongs to tenants.
deeper.stakes: Mixing deposits with operating funds is commingling. In NY that can mean DOS discipline and tenant lawsuits.
deeper.exam: 6 or more units: interest-bearing account, interest to tenant, landlord may keep 1% per year.

blocks.caption: Click through the rules every NY residential manager applies: 1-month deposit cap, 14-day return, $20 screening fee cap, late fee limits, notice periods, stabilization, Good Cause, and the FARE Act.

blocks.q: Sal's management agreement with Hudson & Hart lets the firm sign leases, hire contractors up to $5,000, and collect rents. The firm is Sal's:
c: Special agent
Universal agent
Subagent
General agent
blocks.x: Authority over an ongoing range of matters for one principal makes the manager a general agent. A special agent handles one task, like a single sale.

blocks.html: The owner is the lessor (landlord) and the tenant the lessee. A one-year apartment lease or a ten-year store lease is a tenancy for years: a definite start and end date, ending without notice (though NY rent rules may require renewal or notice). When a tenant must leave, the landlord uses court process: an actual eviction by a marshal or sheriff after a judgment. If the landlord's failure (no heat, no water) makes the space unlivable and the tenant leaves, that is constructive eviction, and the tenant may stop owing rent.
blocks.casual: The owner is the lessor (landlord) and the tenant is the lessee. A one-year apartment lease or a ten-year store lease is a tenancy for years: clear start and end date, and it ends without notice (though NY rent rules may require renewal or notice). When a tenant has to go, the landlord uses the courts: an actual eviction by a marshal or sheriff after a judgment. If the landlord's failure (no heat, no water) makes the place unlivable and the tenant leaves, that's constructive eviction, and the tenant may stop owing rent.

deeper.plain: Leases with fixed dates end on their own. Landlords evict through court; landlords who make a place unlivable can lose the rent.
deeper.picture: Actual eviction is the landlord pushing the tenant out the front door with a court order. Constructive eviction is the landlord letting the house fall apart until the tenant has to walk out.
deeper.street: In January the boiler at a Bushwick building dies and stays dead for three weeks. A tenant moves out. She can argue constructive eviction and stop paying rent from when she left.
deeper.stakes: Lockouts or self-help evictions are illegal in NY. Neglect can cost an owner rent and invite lawsuits.
deeper.exam: Tenancy for years has definite dates. Actual eviction needs a court judgment and a marshal or sheriff. Constructive eviction requires the tenant to leave.

head: Market
What the manager focuses on
rows: Tenant mix, Class A/B/C positioning, lease escalations, building systems (HVAC, elevators), space planning for tenants
Anchor stores that draw traffic, percentage leases, common area maintenance (CAM) charges, merchandising mix
Leasing and turnover, rent collection, NY rent regulation and Good Cause, repairs, HPD rules in NYC
Manager works for the board, not individual owners: budgets, maintenance or common charges, house rules, board packages, staff
A planned unit development (PUD) has a homeowners association; the manager maintains common areas and collects HOA dues

deeper.plain: Each property type has its own priorities: tenant mix in offices, traffic in retail, turnover and regulation in apartments, boards in co-ops.
deeper.picture: Same job title, different sport. Office is chess, retail is a fair, residential is a busy diner, co-ops are a committee meeting.
deeper.street: Evelyn's Flushing mall manager chases a grocery anchor to pull shoppers. Her Midtown office manager tracks HVAC complaints and escalations. Kim's co-op manager answers to her board, not to any one shareholder.
deeper.stakes: Run a co-op like an apartment building and the manager may take orders from the wrong person. Ignore anchors and the whole retail center can die.
deeper.exam: Condo and co-op managers work for the board. Retail uses anchors and percentage leases. PUD managers collect HOA dues.

blocks.title: Managing in the city
blocks.html: NYC residential buildings with 3 or more units register with HPD every year, and a 6-unit Astoria walk-up built before 1974 is very likely rent stabilized. A manager who raises a stabilized rent beyond Rent Guidelines Board increases creates overcharge liability for the owner.
blocks.casual: Managing in the city: NYC residential buildings with 3 or more units register with HPD every year. And a 6-unit Astoria walk-up built before 1974 is very likely rent stabilized. A manager who bumps a stabilized rent beyond what the Rent Guidelines Board allows creates overcharge liability for the owner.

deeper.plain: In NYC, register most buildings with HPD each year and check whether units are rent stabilized before raising rents.
deeper.picture: A stabilized apartment comes with a rent speed limit. Go over it and the ticket goes to the owner.
deeper.street: Sal's 31st Avenue building has six units and was built in 1931. Before renewing a lease, Hudson & Hart checks the registration history and applies only the Rent Guidelines Board increase.
deeper.stakes: An overcharge can mean refunds to tenants, often with interest and penalties. Missed HPD registration can block an owner from certain court actions.
deeper.exam: Pre-1974 buildings with 6 or more units in NYC are typically stabilized. HPD registration for 3+ unit buildings.

blocks.html: The syllabus list is long because the job is: supervising staff, general accounting principles and monthly and yearly reports, building systems (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, elevators, waterproofing, boilers and chillers), landlord-tenant law, leasing and space planning, advertising, codes, union negotiations (many NYC building workers are 32BJ members), purchasing, finance and market trends, construction, and environmental issues.
blocks.casual: The syllabus list is long because the job is long: supervising staff, basic accounting with monthly and annual reports, building systems (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, elevators, waterproofing, boilers and chillers), landlord-tenant law, leasing and space planning, advertising, codes, union negotiations (lots of NYC building workers are 32BJ members), purchasing, finance and market trends, construction, and environmental issues.

deeper.plain: A good manager knows a little about everything in a building and the law around it.
deeper.picture: A manager is a hospital administrator for a building: not the surgeon, but has to understand every department.
deeper.street: Ray inspects a Bay Ridge co-op and flags a failing boiler. The manager gets three bids, checks the 32BJ contract on overtime for the porters during the swap, and updates the capital budget for the board.
deeper.stakes: Gaps in any one area, like union rules or environmental issues, can mean grievances, fines, or safety hazards.
deeper.exam: Expect a list question asking which skill is part of property management. Union negotiations and building systems both are.

blocks.html: The manager's obligations to the owner come down to four things: meet the owner's goals (income now or value later), keep the property to agreed maintenance criteria, plan for the future of the project (capital needs, repositioning), and report honestly and on time.
blocks.casual: What the manager owes the owner comes down to four things: hit the owner's goals (income now or value later), keep the place to the agreed maintenance criteria, plan for the future of the project (capital needs, repositioning), and report honestly and on time.

deeper.plain: Meet the owner's goals, maintain the building, plan ahead, and report honestly.
deeper.picture: Four legs of a table: goals, upkeep, planning, reporting. Lose one and the table wobbles.
deeper.street: Sal wants steady income and a building he can leave to his daughter. Hudson & Hart's annual plan sets a reserve for a roof replacement expected in a few years and sends Sal a monthly statement every month on time.
deeper.stakes: Missed reports and surprise capital bills destroy trust and often end management contracts.
deeper.exam: Four obligations: owner's goals, maintenance criteria, future of the project, reporting.

deeper.plain: Professional designations show training and experience, but none of them replace a New York license.
deeper.picture: Designations are belts in martial arts. The license is permission to step on the mat at all.
deeper.street: Kim's co-op hires a manager with a CMCA. Evelyn's office portfolio is run by a CPM. The management firm itself holds an AMO. All of them still need NY broker licensing for leasing and rent collection.
deeper.stakes: Hiring based on letters alone while ignoring licensing can leave an owner with an unlicensed manager collecting rents.
deeper.exam: IREM: CPM, ARM, AMO (AMO is for firms). BOMI: RPA. CAMICB: CMCA for community associations.

blocks.html: Most managers start as leasing agents, assistant managers, or resident managers and earn designations through courses and experience. In New York, the license comes first whenever the work includes leasing or collecting rent for others.
blocks.casual: Most managers start out as leasing agents, assistant managers or resident managers, and earn designations through courses and experience. In New York, the license comes first whenever the work includes leasing or collecting rent for others.

deeper.plain: Start in an entry-level role, build up, but get licensed before you lease or collect rent for others.
deeper.picture: It's a ladder: leasing agent, assistant manager, manager, then designations. The license is the first rung if you're touching leases or rent.
deeper.street: Jordan spends a year leasing apartments in Sal's building and others under Diane. Later Jordan takes IREM classes toward the ARM.
deeper.stakes: Starting work before licensing exposes you and the firm to unlicensed activity complaints.
deeper.exam: License before leasing or rent collection for others. Designations are optional; licensing is not.

blocks.q: Kim Alvarez, president of an Upper West Side co-op board, hires a managing agent. To whom does the managing agent owe fiduciary duties?
c: Each individual shareholder
The co-op corporation through its board
The building staff union
Prospective purchasers
blocks.x: The managing agent is hired by and works for the co-op corporation, acting through the board. Individual shareholders are not the principal.

story.title: The Handshake
story.setting: Sal's building, 31st Avenue, Astoria, a cold Saturday

beats.text: Five percent of the rents, you handle everything. We shake on it.
I'd love to, Sal. But collecting rent for you for a fee is brokerage. It has to go through my broker, in writing.
My super Vinnie collects rent and he's got no license.
Vinnie's your employee, lives in the building, works only for you. That's the resident manager exception. I'm not your employee.

check.q: Why can Vinnie collect rent without a license?
c: He's been doing it for years
He is the owner's salaried resident employee working only for that owner
Rent under $3,000 doesn't count
Supers are always exempt
check.x: The exception covers the owner's own on-site employee acting for that owner. A super paid by an outside firm per lease would not qualify.

beats.text: Monday. Diane slides a management agreement across the desk to Sal.
Property, term, what we can do without calling you, the fee, reports, insurance, your goals, and how either of us can walk away.
What's this, 'authority up to $3,000 per repair without owner approval'?
That's management authority. Above that, we call you. We're your general agent, Sal. We run the building, but we answer to you.
And you're loyal to me, not the tenants?
We owe you every fiduciary duty. We owe the tenants honesty, the law, and fair housing. Both at once.
beats.tag: Fiduciary to owner, fair to tenants

beats.text: One more thing, Sal. Your building was built in 1928 and has six units. It's almost certainly rent stabilized.
So no 20 percent increase on 3B?
Not unless you'd like to refund it later with triple damages. Sign here, Sal. Then we fix your boiler.

board.prompt: Draft the nine headings of Sal's management agreement. Under each, write one specific term you'd propose.

facts.text: Property management operates real estate to meet the owner's goals, usually the best net income over time while preserving the asset's value.
A manager's functions: marketing and leasing, rent and deposits, tenant relations, maintenance, accounting and reports, compliance, and risk management.
Leasing or collecting rent for others for a fee is brokerage (RPL 440): a management company needs a broker license, and a salesperson's agreements and fees go through the firm.
A resident manager or super employed by the owner, working only for that owner, needs no license; the exception ends once he works for a second owner for a fee.
A super paid per apartment rented by an outside management firm is doing licensed brokerage without a license.
A management agreement makes the property manager a general agent of the owner (a listing broker is a special agent).
As a fiduciary, the manager owes the owner obedience, loyalty, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting and reasonable care.
The management agreement should be written, must be if it runs over a year, and covers property, term, authority, reports, fee, accounting, insurance, owner duties and termination.
Security deposits go in a separate account, never mixed with operating funds; with 6 or more units it must earn interest for the tenant, less a 1% landlord fee.
The owner is the lessor (landlord) and the tenant is the lessee.
A lease with definite start and end dates is a tenancy for years and ends without notice.
Actual eviction is removal by a marshal or sheriff after a judgment; constructive eviction is when the landlord's failure makes the space unlivable and the tenant leaves.
Retail management centers on anchor stores that draw traffic, percentage leases and CAM charges; office on tenant mix, class and escalations.
A condo or co-op managing agent works for the board (the corporation or association), not individual owners.
A planned unit development has a homeowners association; its manager maintains common areas and collects HOA dues.
NYC residential buildings with 3 or more units register with HPD yearly, and raising a stabilized rent beyond RGB increases creates overcharge liability for the owner.
The manager's obligations to the owner: meet the owner's goals, maintain the property to agreed standards, plan for its future, and report honestly and on time.
The CPM (and ARM, AMO) designations come from IREM; RPA from BOMI; CMCA for community association managers; in NY the license comes first.

lessons.title: Budgets, Rent Rolls, Maintenance, and Risk
lessons.tagline: Good managers run buildings on paper first: a budget, a rent roll, a maintenance plan, and a report the owner can read.
objectives: Distinguish operating, capital reserve, and stabilized budgets
Read a rent roll and compute NOI from it
Classify maintenance as preventive, corrective, routine, or deferred
Apply the four risk management strategies
Describe a management proposal and a property management report

blocks.title: Hudson & Hart, first month on Sal's building
blocks.html: Sal calls Jordan: "Why are you asking me for $2,000 a month for a 'reserve'? The boiler works. Spend money when it breaks." Jordan knows the boiler is 26 years old and the roof was last done in 2009. How does Jordan show Sal, in numbers, why the reserve matters?
blocks.casual: Sal calls Jordan: "Why are you asking me for $2,000 a month for a 'reserve'? The boiler works. Spend money when it breaks." Jordan knows the boiler's 26 years old and the roof was last done in 2009. So how does Jordan show Sal, with actual numbers, why the reserve matters?

deeper.plain: Big repairs are coming whether the owner likes it or not. Saving a bit each month beats a huge surprise bill.
deeper.picture: It's like putting money aside each month for a car you know will need new tires next winter, instead of scrambling when the tread is gone.
deeper.street: Sal's old-school instinct is "fix it when it breaks." Jordan pulls the boiler's install date from the plate in the basement and shows Sal two quotes: $45,000 for a boiler, $60,000 for a roof.
deeper.stakes: Without reserves, a January boiler failure means no heat, HPD violations, angry tenants and an emergency loan at a bad rate.
deeper.exam: Questions about "reserves" or "replacement" point to the capital reserve budget, not the operating budget.

head: Budget
Covers
Example in Sal's building
rows: One year of expected income and day-to-day expenses
Rents, vacancy, taxes, insurance, fuel, water, repairs, super's pay, management fee
Money set aside for big replacements and improvements
Boiler ($45,000 in about 4 years), roof ($60,000 in about 6 years)
A multi-year forecast that smooths income and expenses into a typical (normalized) year
Average 5 years of costs so a one-time year does not distort value or planning

deeper.plain: One budget runs this year, one saves for big future replacements, and one smooths out several years into a typical year.
deeper.picture: Operating budget is your monthly grocery list. Capital reserve is the savings jar for a new fridge. Stabilized budget is your average spend over five years so one wild year doesn't fool you.
deeper.street: Sal's operating budget covers fuel, water and the super. His capital reserve saves toward the $45,000 boiler and $60,000 roof. When a buyer appraises the building, a stabilized budget averages the year Sal paid for a one-time lead abatement so it doesn't drag down value.
deeper.stakes: Mix the budgets up and a one-time cost looks permanent, or a big replacement gets treated like a monthly bill. Both skew value and planning.
deeper.exam: Operating = one year, day to day. Capital reserve = big replacements. Stabilized = normalized multi-year forecast.

blocks.html: Expenses come in kinds. A fixed expense stays the same regardless of occupancy (property taxes, insurance). A variable expense moves with use and occupancy (utilities, repairs, supplies, turnover painting). A capital expense buys or replaces a long-lived component (new boiler, new roof, new windows): it comes out of reserves and is not an operating expense when calculating NOI.
blocks.casual: Expenses come in flavors. A fixed expense stays the same no matter how many units are filled (property taxes, insurance). A variable expense moves with use and occupancy (utilities, repairs, supplies, painting at turnover). A capital expense buys or replaces something long-lived (new boiler, new roof, new windows). It comes out of reserves and isn't an operating expense when you figure NOI.

deeper.plain: Some costs never change, some rise and fall with use, and some are big once-in-a-while replacements.
deeper.picture: Fixed is your phone plan. Variable is your electric bill. Capital is buying a new phone every few years.
deeper.street: When unit 1B sits empty, Sal's property tax and insurance don't budge, but the turnover painting and the extra utility use for showings do. Replacing all the windows next year is capital, paid from reserves.
